[8] E-mail: prensa@mindef.gov.ar Web: www.mindef.gov.ar In Union and Freedom 3 Presentation 4 The economic, social and political crisis of 2001 revealed the limits of growth based on financial speculation, making it clear that we had to return to the path of economic development with social inclusion, rebuilding our industrial structure, paying special attention in this phase to new technologies and returning to the world from Latin America and particularly, from South America

[9] This is how José de San Martín, Manuel Belgrano, José Artigas, Bernardo O'Higgins, José Sucre, Simón Bolívar, and many others understood it when they maintained that independence required the efforts of all the men and women of America

[10] Therefore, the future of Argentina's Bicentennial is irrevocably linked to the future of the region to which it belongs: we will be able to occupy our rightful place in the world, with the region and from the region, and not turning our backs on it

[11] Any external aggression against a country in the region in pursuit of its resources also affects our country's strategic interests

[12] South America is a land of human and cultural potential and enormous natural wealth

[13] South America holds 44 percent of the planet's natural water reserves, 25 percent of its agricultural land, and approximately 26 percent of its fossil fuel reserves, including gas and oil

[14] Therefore, the Armed Forces must be alert to the challenge of their sovereign protection, which is that of the entire region

[15] The restoration of democracy in 1983 was an achievement for all Argentines

[16] Despite the complexity of the transition in those early years and the significant economic difficulties we had to overcome, 27 years after that milestone, we can say that together we have managed to consolidate the institutional order as the only way to channel our collective aspirations and differences

[17] Today we understand that this order is not a sufficient condition to meet the needs of our citizens, especially those who suffer the most, but we are convinced that it is a necessary and fundamental condition

[18] We also believe that the country's progress lies in its ability to generate jobs and knowledge

[19] In recent years, the Argentine Republic has embarked on a sustained path of economic recovery based on a development model centered on work, production, and value generation

[20] The National Defense System, like other strategic areas of the Nation, was neglected during the 1990s as part of a state reform process that assumed that all public expenditure was inherently inefficient and could not constitute any form of investment: whether productive, technological, or even social

[21] This meant a growing gap between the defense sector's organization and deployment, and the budget allocated for its maintenance

[22] This fallaciously economic logic was characterized by the absence of an effective defense policy framework that would establish political objectives and conduct the necessary reforms to adapt the Ministry of Defense and the Armed Forces to new regional and global realities and, consequently, to the nation's defense needs

[23] At the same time, the research and development subsystem, as well as the defense oriented production sector, was dismantled, with many of our country's leading companies being privatized in some cases or liquidated in others

[24] For future generations and for the generations that came before us, in this Bicentennial we must commit ourselves, convinced, following the motto of General José de San Martín, not to take up arms against our people or our Latin American brothers and sisters

[25] Our aspiration is to consolidate a defense that contributes from its place to national and regional development, integrated into society, and contributing its benefits to building a better quality of life for all Argentines

[26] Buenos Aires, December 2010 Dr

[27] Cristina Fernández de Kirchner President of the Nation Defense is a task that involves all actors in national life and must therefore be an important part of the public agenda

[28] Defense contributes to technological-industrial development and this contributes to Defense

[29] This was understood by political leaders such as Nicolás Avellaneda, Marcelo T. de Alvear, Juan Domingo Perón and Arturo Frondizi, and illustrious citizens by military profession, such as Enrique Mosconi, Francisco de Arteaga, Manuel Savio, Segundo Storni and Juan Ignacio San Martín

[30] Reviving the vision that inspired them, the strategic decision was made to recover the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex (CINAR), the former Military Aircraft Factory (FAdeA), and to support the men and women who daily contribute their knowledge to strengthening research, science, and technology integrated into the defense industry

[31] This synergy must be strengthened by incorporating universities and research centers throughout the country, as well as small and medium-sized industries, to contribute to the generation of value chains based on cutting-edge technologies such as aerospace, naval, nuclear, and ICT, among others

[32] The men and women, in uniform and civilians, who carry out our national defense every day are full citizens who have chosen the military profession

[33] Like Belgrano and the people of Jujuy, who made a tactical retreat to confront the royalists in Tucumán

[34] The military instrument, comprised of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, has the primary mission of warding off and repelling any external state military aggression that endangers our sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the lives and property of our inhabitants

[35] This central role is assumed from a defensive strategic position that, through its autonomous dimension, communicates to the world that Argentina has not renounced its legitimate defense, as established in Article 51 of the United Nations Charter. From its cooperative perspective, it understands that in the future, just as during the independence processes, the defense of our vital interests and strategic resources will be a collective regional task

[36] In this sense, we will not be indifferent to external aggression against a country in the region

[37] Or like San Martín and the people of Cuyo, forging the cannons, uniforms, and flag of the nation, today our citizens in uniform stand side by side, across the country, supporting the community through health campaigns or in situations of natural disasters

[38] Our Armed Forces have also been internationally praised for their humanitarian work in Haiti, Bolivia, Cyprus, Chile, the former Yugoslavia, the Middle East, and Africa

[39] To achieve these objectives, in compliance with a clear legal mandate, the Ministry of Defense, under precise directives from the Commander-in-Chief, embarked on a process of structural transformation that sought to scale and articulate the Defense System to optimize its contribution to the development of the Argentine State

[40] This involved adapting and operationalizing the entire legal, political, and institutional framework of the sector to diagnose dysfunctions and promote the necessary changes

[41] One of the many outcomes of this process was the approval, by then President Néstor Kirchner, of the National Defense Planning Cycle and the issuance of the National Defense Policy Directive (DPDN) by President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner

[42] These initiatives represented the definitive implementation of the capabilities-based planning model in defense policy, thus overcoming the obsolete conflict hypothesis approach

[43] To promote greater effectiveness and efficiency in defense management, the administration of material and human resources was optimized, seeking to maximize the generation and maintenance of military capabilities determined by strategic planning

[44] The objective of this transformation was to articulate an integrated management system that would allow the capabilities approved in planning to be translated into human, material, and infrastructure resources in an effective, efficient, and transparent manner

[45] Meanwhile, regarding the educational subsystem, a profound regulatory, organizational, and curricular reform was implemented, and aspects of institutional culture were also addressed

[46] Another objective of this transformation was to generate better conditions of equality between women and men working in the Defense System, adopting various actions related to professional relationships and the possibility of accessing and remaining in the workforce under conditions of equal treatment

[47] In this sense, the comprehensive reform of the military justice system was paradigmatic, as it was regulated by a Military Justice Code that did not comply with national legislation and current international regulations

[48] Among the highlights of this reform are the elimination of military jurisdiction for the prosecution of crimes committed by members of the armed forces, the definitive elimination of the death penalty from the Argentine legal system, and the establishment of a joint justice system

[49] Since defense policy is also part of Argentina's foreign policy, an intense policy of dialogue and international integration was undertaken—especially in the South American region—aimed at strengthening ties, improving mutual trust-building measures, and developing common projects, thereby eliminating any remaining traces of discord that might exist between our peoples

[50] Examples of this include the successful work carried out by our men and women in MINUSTAH, collaborating with the recovery of the Republic of Haiti, the establishment of the Combined Peacekeeping Force "Cruz del Sur" with the Republic of Chile, the Combined Engineer Company "Don José de San Martín" with the Republic of Peru, and the sustained and growing progress seen in the South American Defense Council (CDS

[51] The advances described are just examples of the profound reform that the Argentine Republic has been able to consolidate in its Defense System since the restoration of democracy in

[52] This was largely possible thanks to the broad consensus reached among political and social forces in this field, embodied in a set of regulations approved by various administrations

[53] This White Paper, as established by numerous multilateral bodies in which our country participates, constitutes in itself a measure of confidence and promotion of peace among nations

[54] But it is also an official document that aims to clearly show the characteristics of the Defense System, analyzing it from its historical formation to the most recent reforms

[55] Through this document, we hope that every citizen can understand the purpose and reason for which public resources are transferred to this sector of the State

[56] With the understanding that the development of state policies must be the product of a plural and federal process of discussion, this 2010 White Paper on Defense was accompanied by a discussion and consultation process that, with the methodological assistance of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), organized more than ten reflection activities throughout the country throughout

[57] These activities, summarized in an appendix to this book and detailed on a separate website (www.libroblanco2010.gob.ar), attracted a significant portion of the specialized academic community in Argentina and the region, as well as journalists, legislators, students, and the general public

[58] This document, which updates the 1999 White Paper on Defense, is structured in three parts: - The first develops an analysis of the geostrategic characteristics relevant to the Argentine Republic, starting from a global perspective to a regional one, culminating in a chapter that presents the strategic position and attitude of the Argentine Republic in this world and how-to the right extent of its potential - it intends to positively influence the international scene

[59] Among other things, the document presents the characteristics of the strategic defensive positioning adopted by our country, within the framework of regional cooperation that contributes to consolidating Latin America as a zone of peace

[60] The second part presents the characteristics of the Argentine Defense System: its historical conformation, its normative structure and its organizational architecture

[61] The third and final part describes the transformation process that has taken place since the publication of the last White Paper

[62] The publication of this White Paper is taking place within the framework of our country's Bicentennial, a moment of particular and symbolic importance for a debate that transcends commonplaces and allows the Defense sector to assess where we are, how we are doing, where we've come from, and where we're going

[63] And in this way, we can develop policies that transcend the circumstantial passage of a single administration, thus becoming a consolidated state policy

[64] Buenos Aires, December

[65] One of those actions carried out by Dr. Garré, and which I have the opportunity to present today, is this 2010 White Paper on Defense

[66] This Bicentennial White Paper, as the Minister points out in her prologue, updates the one produced in 1999 and presents to our society and to the concert of nations the characteristics and priorities of our defense policy, our country's strategic stance in the face of its interpretation of the world, and the tenor and scope of the main transformations that have taken place in the defense system since the publication of the last White Paper

[67] This Book is a reflection of what has been done, but also a path to the future

[68] Therefore, from this position where I have the honor of working today, the starting point will be the path we have taken, consolidating reforms that have been structural and that I am convinced will place our military instrument in a more suitable condition to defend our vital and strategic interests, while respecting human rights

[69] In this regard, within the framework of the Defense Planning Cycle, the design of the military instrument that our country must systematically develop, which human and material resources will be required for the National Defense of Argentina's Bicentennial, will be presented for the first time in

[70] To this end, the National Science, Technology, and Innovation System will play a crucial role in the development of our future Armed Forces

[71] This progressive construction will be possible thanks to the recovery of the former Military Aircraft Factory, now known as FADEA; the Almirante Storni Shipyard (formerly Domecq García) and TANDANOR, which now comprise the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex (CINAR); and the significant progress and support provided to the defense system by Military Manufacturing

[72] President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner has given me the honor and responsibility of taking over the management of the Ministry of Defense after five years of profound transformations implemented by Dr. Nilda Garré, based on the guidance and leadership successively defined for this strategic sector by the President herself and former President Néstor Kirchner

[73] This Bicentennial must be the first step toward the definitive consolidation of modern Armed Forces, trained and ready to face the challenges that the future holds for our country

[74] We are not taking this first step in a vacuum; we are taking it on the basis of hard work that has not been limited solely to the National Defense System; we are taking it on the basis of a new model of economic development with social inclusion, with an industry that has recovered its productive capacities, and with a society that, with justice and memory, is moving toward a prosperous future

[130] Retired and pensioned personnel 382 Chapter XXIV: ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY Annex Part I Chapter I International terrorism, one of the most significant current threats to global peace and security, is a phenomenon of transnational nature and capacity for global impact that has demonstrated the ineffectiveness of military means for its resolution, requiring instead comprehensive and multilateral actions

[131] Argentina, which suffered this scourge in 1992 and 1994, understands the importance of international cooperation in addressing this problem

[132] Environmental deterioration, along with the failure to reach basic agreements on habitat protection, underscores the resistance to change and the limited capacity for negotiation that can lead the international system to stagnate

[133] Globally, the distribution of and access to natural resources (primarily food and energy) will be uneven in the coming decades, and local and regional deficits will arise, increasing the likelihood of internal social instability or disagreements between states that could lead to conflict

[134] It is also foreseeable that the frequency, scale and duration of humanitarian crises will increase simultaneously

[135] The levels of inequality in wealth distribution are disturbing worldwide and particularly dramatic in Latin America

[136] While a general reduction in global poverty is expected in the coming decades, inequality of opportunity between regions—particularly evident in matters of health, nutrition, education, and access to new technologies—is likely to deepen global inequality and could fuel future conflicts

[137] The global security agenda has been besieged by significant problems that generally occur within or across states and can have detrimental effects on the multilateral system

[138] These include criminal networks, human trafficking, piracy, and drug trafficking, among others

[139] These scourges, which for Argentina constitute internal security problems, have not generally proven amenable to resolution through military means, although in some latitudes direct intervention by the armed forces has been called for

[140] Thus, a good part of the challenges to international security that currently arise come from: a) transnational phenomena of a varied nature, the most important of which are transnational terrorism and organized crime: drug, arms and human trafficking, and piracy; Part I Chapter I b) crises or conflicts of diverse origin within States that threaten to overflow borders and destabilize regions (ethnic, cultural and religious tensions, weakness of the State apparatus, famines or health emergencies); and c) climate change and ecological and environmental deterioration could also cause disruptions in the international arena, while as a consequence they could affect food production or lead to the extinction of freshwater courses, thus provoking massive migratory flows or conflicts over food resources and drinking water

[141] The realization that increased interdependence has made the phenomenon of international security more complex has increasingly led actors in the global system to agree on the need for comprehensive and multilateral approaches to its core issues

[142] There is growing international awareness that it is essential to address the causes, not just the effects, of such scourges, within the framework of the necessary joint efforts of nations to confront and overcome common challenges

[143] Part I Assessment of the Regional Scenario The Latin American scenario in terms of international defense and security has experienced structural transformations over the last two decades due to causes of various origins: some exogenous derived from the disappearance of the bipolar order of the Cold War and others endogenous linked to the construction of regional integration processes and, as a consequence, the progressive disappearance of historical hypotheses of regional conflicts

[144] There is a clear difference in the region between interstate security issues and transnational security issues, the latter being affected by non-state actors that operate and impact across borders

[145] While the past two decades have generally seen an improvement in interstate relations, internal security conditions have simultaneously deteriorated due to a growing expansion of mutable challenges in almost all Latin American nations

[146] The main threats to the security and integrity of Latin American nations have tended to shift from the traditional axis of conflicts between states to another, dominated by transnational crimes characterized by their particular corrosive dynamics of state capabilities and foundations

[147] From the perspective of interstate relations, the current level of security in South America is unprecedented

[148] This situation is the result of the maturing dialogue, cooperation, and consensus-building that have been achieved, conditions that distinguish the region—despite some specific distortions—as one of the most stable and predictable in the world

[149] The improvement in interstate relations is the result of a political and economic process that began in the mid-1980s, anchored in external and global causes and internal and regional factors

[150] On the external level, the end of the bipolar confrontation and its impact on the regional geopolitical reality are being considered

[151] Domestically, the restoration of the rule of law throughout the region is seen as a major development, and the establishment of mechanisms to guarantee certain recent events, such as the planned use of military bases in a country in the subcontinent by extra-regional forces, or the attack by one country in the region on irregular forces in another country in the region, have generated some disturbance

[152] However, the actions of UNASUR and its Defense Council contributed significantly to positively addressing these episodes

[160] These factors synergistically promoted a dynamic of general détente and the beginning of interstate cooperation

[161] This led to a gradual decline in perceptions of mutual military threats and the construction of new spaces for integration—initially on the commercial level—which positively contributed to the consolidation of bilateral and multilateral mutual trust-building measures

[162] South America also has one of the lowest levels of defense spending in the world

[163] While in most countries in the region the bulk of spending is allocated to personnel and operations, some states have undertaken efforts to modernize and acquire weapons systems, primarily related to the need to technologically update obsolete equipment and improve surveillance and control of sovereign spaces

[164] As a result, the current defense and security landscape in Latin America is characterized by: A widespread commitment to preserving the region as a zone free of weapons of mass destruction

[165] The regional status of a zone free of nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons was consolidated through multiple regional declarations, resolutions of the Organization of American States, subregional organizations such as MERCOSUR, and various international agreements

[166] The strengthening of international law as a mechanism for the peaceful resolution of disputes

[167] Diplomatic consultation alternatives for the peaceful and negotiated resolution of disputes and conflicts between states were consolidated, with an explicit rejection of military alternatives

[168] The consolidation of defensive strategic positions

[169] Policies guided by the principle of self-defense and defensive concepts, as stated in Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, were consolidated throughout almost the entire region

[170] “There have been few international wars involving Latin American states in almost two centuries of independence

[171] …) even if we include civil wars, Latin America has enjoyed relative peace

[172] …) the peace of the region is most clearly seen on a map

[173] Examine a map of Latin America in 1840 and you will see that the general boundaries (…) are surprisingly similar to those of today: no politically recognized state has disappeared as a result of the conquest”

[178] Chapter II Part I Increasing confidence- and security-building measures

[179] A quantitative and qualitative increase in these measures is observed at both the bilateral and multilateral levels

[180] Two levels can be distinguished: the political and the military

[181] At the political level, there are notable actions and initiatives to promote transparency regarding military spending (through the participation of countries in the region in the International Standardized Report on Military Expenditures or the Register of Conventional Arms Transfers, both of the United Nations; or the Inter-American Convention on Transparency in the Acquisition of Conventional Arms, within the OAS

[182] At the military level, there have been fluid contacts between the region's Armed Forces, with extensive practice of combined binational and multinational military exercises, as well as initiatives for military cooperation and complementarity

[183] An example of the latter is the establishment of the Binational Peacekeeping Force "Cruz del Sur" between Argentina and Chile, and the Binational Engineering Company "Don José de San Martín" between Argentina and Peru, both initiatives aimed at participating in United Nations Peacekeeping Operations

[184] The widespread commitment to United Nations Peacekeeping Operations

[185] The region provides around 10% of the personnel for United Nations Peacekeeping Operations deployed worldwide

[186] Furthermore, there is a growing regional commitment to these operations, as demonstrated by the United Nations Stabilization Mission in Haiti (MINUSTAH), where the bulk of the contingent is provided by countries in the region

[187] The orientation of fiscal efforts towards economic and social development

[188] Compared to other regions, South America has one of the lowest levels of defense spending

[253] Consequently, Argentina has signed all international treaties that prohibit the production, development, and stockpiling of any type of weapon of mass destruction, actively participating in the non-proliferation regime, consolidating its role as a responsible actor, and rejecting interventionist practices that are contrary to good coexistence in the international community

[254] The Argentine State adopts a strategic conception and attitude that finds in the concept of self-defense—explicit in Article 51 of the United Nations Charter—the essential and organizing criterion on which its military instrument is structured

[255] Within this framework, Argentina is positioning itself in the scenarios described, seeking—to the extent possible—to positively influence the world

[256] The strategic asset to be defended for foreign and defense policy is peace

[257] Argentina has been and continues to be a signatory and promoter of numerous trust-building and conflict resolution mechanisms related to the control of conventional weapons and weapons of mass destruction, transparency, and respect for human rights

[258] Its guiding principle is to preserve Latin America as a zone of peace and to project this space as a model of coexistence for the rest of the world

[259] The Argentine Republic maintains a defensive model that rejects offensive policies and attitudes that project power toward third countries. This implies that it will not initiate military action unless its vital interests are affected

[260] Likewise, this strategic concept, which guides both the Armed Forces and their military operations, must reflect the intention of a State not to project a threat to the territory of another State

[261] Defense policy, force design, and the forecasting of the employment and evolution of the military instrument are structured according to this principle

[262] This model, entirely predictable in terms of strategic conception and entirely defensive in terms of design, assumes that the mission of national defense is limited to warding off and repelling—through the use of the Armed Forces—all external state military aggression in order to permanently guarantee and safeguard sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and the life and liberty of its inhabitants

[263] The Argentine conception is also based on the recognition of the importance of interstate cooperation and multilateralism in this area, as genuine complementary instruments of self-defense policy

[264] In this sense, in an increasingly interconnected world, Argentina views its defense in the dual dimension of autonomy, on the one hand, and cooperation, on the other

[265] This implies that its force design and non-offensive capabilities are linked to and complement its multilateral commitments

[266] In this spirit, and within the framework of the Union of South American Nations (UNASUR), Argentina actively participated in the creation of the South American Defense Council (CDS

[267] Since the peace and security of nations are increasingly interdependent realities and objectives, the national defense policy recognizes and adheres to the postulates of the Argentine Navy's Sea Fleet Ships

[272] Just as the Argentine Republic has assumed its responsibilities to contribute to the United Nations Collective Security System, its defense policy is also committed to strengthening and consolidating the military and defense cooperation policies and practices in South America

[273] Seeking conditions that consolidate the maintenance of peace, it is Argentina's state policy to deepen regional defense cooperation and, at the same time, advance—according to the wishes of neighboring states—in the construction of a subregional defense system that transcends the levels of mutual trust already achieved and allows for access to qualitatively higher levels

[274] This policy faithfully reflects the commitment and integrationist vocation of the Argentine Republic

[275] Argentina views its defense policy as a contributing factor to its national development strategy

[276] Within this framework, the process of strengthening the defense industry will continue through the development, management, and supervision of all defense research, development, and production projects

[277] Therefore, cooperation will continue and be deepened, within the framework of the National Science, Technology and Innovation System, with other state agencies that carry out or may carry out useful research and development

[280] Part I Chapter III Thus, it is considered strategic to advance the research, development and application of aerospace, nuclear and cyberspace-related technologies from the National Defense System, within the framework of the provisions of the National Constitution and the multiple current agreements of which the country is a signatory

[281] Aerospace and cyberspace technologies are critical contributions to achieving the intended effects of a defensive strategy

[282] These are considered essential for providing early strategic warning against potential external state military aggression, and for effectively conducting military operations and successfully repelling such aggression

[283] These technologies also contribute to the effective control of the Nation's land, sea, and aerospace spaces

[284] Regarding aerospace technology specifically, Argentina aspires to advance and achieve independence in the development and manufacture of satellite launchers, as well as in the design and construction of communications and command and control satellites

[285] The development and manufacture of unmanned aerial platforms is also relevant to the defense industry and to domestic industry

[286] With regard to cyberspace and its use in defense, mastery of cyberspace is not only essential for the exercise of command and control and for the networking of the system, but also for repelling and warding off external state military threats that may arise using so-called cyberspace as a means of execution or targeting it

[287] To this end, the development of an organic-functional core, with a specific doctrine, is a challenge for the future of the defense system

[288] The research, development, and manufacturing of nuclear-fueled propulsion systems for military platforms would allow Argentina to take advantage of technological developments in a field in which it has achieved significant development

[289] In addition to being in line with the national strategy for diversifying the energy matrix, from the perspective of surveillance, reconnaissance, and control capabilities, it would allow for exponentially increasing patrol autonomy and stealth in the case of maritime areas under jurisdiction

[290] As previously noted and further explored in Chapter XVII, it is understood that the development of aerospace and nuclear technologies will have very positive effects on the scientific-technological and industrial system, both public and private, due to the externalities they generate

[295] The Argentine Republic deplores, in this regard, the hydrocarbon resource exploration actions undertaken by the United Kingdom in the disputed area. [302] THE DEFENSE SYSTEM The evolution of the defense system of the Argentine Republic has been conditioned by domestic political-institutional transformations and reconfigurations of the international order

[303] Since the restoration of democracy in 1983, internal and external dynamics have led to multiparty consensus on the foundations that should structure the national defense system

[304] As a result of this dynamic, the National Congress passed a set of laws – the National Defense Law, the Internal Security Law, the Voluntary Military Service Law, the Armed Forces Restructuring Law, the National Intelligence Law, and the Comprehensive Reform of the Military Justice System Law – that defined central issues: the missions and architecture of the defense system, the consolidation of the civilian government of defense policy, the distinction between the conceptual spheres of national defense and internal security, and the roles and functions of the Armed Forces

[305] HISTORICAL CONFIGURATION OF THE ARGENTINE DEFENSE SYSTEM The constitution and articulation of any defense system occurs within the framework of the political structure of which it is a part

[306] In the Argentine case, it is closely related to the process of national organization and consolidation of the form of State

[307] This historical process, filled with consensus and debate, advances and counter-advances, can be approached in different periods for better visualization

[308] EMANCIPATION

[309] The May Revolution of 1810 initiated a prolonged armed conflict fought for South American emancipation. The consequence of this, beyond the severance of colonial ties with Spain, was the local dismantling of the viceregal state, a highly centralized political entity that disintegrated into distinct nationalities and, in the case of Argentina, fragmented into a set of new political units, the provinces, which were organized between 1810 and

[310] Initially, the deposition of the last viceroy involved the establishment of a Provisional Government Board that demanded recognition throughout the territory of the then Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata and all the institutions that comprised it

[311] The defense system also recognizes as a starting point the colonial order, whose head was the viceroy, head of the colonial State and Commander-in-Chief of the military forces, on whom a General Commander of Arms and an Inspector of Arms depended

[312] The system had been articulated to respond to the external threat of that time against the Spanish crown (Great Britain and Portugal), for which it had coastal fortresses on both banks of the Río de la Plata and also forts, blockhouses and guards that guarded the internal border, mainly against resistance actions by the indigenous peoples

[313] The system relied on regular troops, that is, professionals, and each city had to provide for the mobilization of residents in "militia" bodies if necessary

[314] At the end of the first decade of the 19th century, the viceregal defensive system was in a deep crisis as a result of the wear and tear caused by the political and military conflicts in the metropolis and by the English invasions of Buenos Aires in 1806 and 1807, which it was unable to repel

[315] In this city, the regular forces had failed against the invader, and the people had to create a citizen army (militiamen) that did not disarm after repelling the invader and became an important actor that channeled the revolutionary mobilization of May

[316] In fact, the First Patriotic Government Board was initially presided over by Cornelio Saavedra, who was head of the Patricios Regiment (a militia corps formed in

[317] Following the Revolution of May 25, 1810, the First Government Junta, among its first provisions, determined on May 28 the creation of the Secretariat of Government and War, with Mariano Moreno in charge, and, by the proclamation of May 29, recognized the militia corps of Buenos Aires as regular forces, elevating their category from battalions to regiments

[318] It is worth highlighting, in terms of the organic evolution of the system in its germinal stage, the creation of the Military General Staff by decree of the First Triumvirate, to which the Weapons Inspection was incorporated

[319] Later, by decree of the Supreme Director Juan Martín de Pueyrredón, the General Staff was created

[320] This period saw the establishment of cannon, rifle and cartridge factories in Buenos Aires, Tucumán and Mendoza, as well as bladed weapons factories in Córdoba

[321] In 1814, the naval Battle of Montevideo took place, a battle that became the culmination of an operational strategic plan that had been drawn up by Carlos de Alvear and led by Guillermo Brown to occupy the last Spanish enclave on the Río de la Plata

[322] This victory is considered the founding milestone of the Argentine Navy

[323] Notwithstanding the milestones mentioned, the precariousness of the defense system must be pointed out, since only the experience of the Army of the Andes (1816-1824), organized and led by General José de San Martín, shows strategic criteria for the creation and development of forces, organization and planning that allowed him to successfully project military power and move the theater of operations away from the Río de la Plata

[324] THE CIVIL WAR AND THE ARGENTINE CONFEDERATION (1820 to 1852) After the victory of the federal leaders Estanislao López (Santa Fe) and Francisco Ramírez (Entre Ríos) over the Supreme Director José Rondeau in the com- Chapter IV Part II Embrace of Maipú

[325] At the end of Cañada de Cepeda, the central authority was dissolved and the provincial powers and armies were organized

[326] That same year, in the Province of Buenos Aires, the then governor Manuel de Sarratea abolished the highest bodies of the Army, the General Staff and the Ministry of War

[327] In 1822, under the government of Martín Rodríguez, with Bernardino Rivadavia as Political Secretary, a new military structure was established, purging its ranks by eliminating senior officers through the so-called retirement and reward laws

[328] The Navy Command was also abolished

[329] This dismantling of the central military organizations gave rise to the creation of the Army of the Province of Buenos Aires

[330] The organic instability of the institutions affected the military bodies, causing a greater number of desertions and a lack of enlisted personnel

[331] To solve the problem, a decree was issued in Buenos Aires in April 1822, which established the recruitment of "vagrants" (those who did not have a "conchabo" (employment certificate), a sort of work certification for an employment relationship

[332] December 1823, a provincial militia law was passed for military recruitment, which was only replaced in 1872 by a national law

[333] In January 1825, the General Constituent Congress of the provinces passed a Fundamental Law that, Chapter IV, Part II, created a national executive power, delegated to the government of Buenos Aires, in charge of managing war and foreign relations

[334] Shortly after, the War against Brazil (1825 – 1828) broke out, on which occasion a federal army was organized

[335] When this war ended in 1828, the army returned and the internal political conflict intensified

[336] The overthrow of the then governor of Buenos Aires, Manuel Dorrego, and his execution, added to the defeat in the Province of Córdoba of Juan Bautista Bustos by General José María Paz, in San Roque, completed the panorama of the intensification of the civil war

[337] Following the signing of the Federal Pact of 1831, a confederation was established in which each province assumed responsibility for its own defense, a principle that prevailed until the fall of Juan Manuel de Rosas in

[338] From 1838, the Confederation faced two of the most important world powers: the French blockade (1838 – 1840) and the Anglo-French blockade (1845 – 1850), during the course of the latter, the Battle of Vuelta de Obligado (November 20, 1845) took place

[339] The uprising against Juan Manuel de Rosas by the governor of Entre Ríos, Justo José de Urquiza, and his formation of the Great Army (made up of forces from Entre Ríos and Corrientes, as well as Brazil and Uruguay) led to Urquiza's victory in the Battle of Caseros

[340] After that battle, a Governors' Agreement was formalized, which led to the convening of a Constituent Congress in the Province of Santa Fe

[341] A few months later, sectors of Buenos Aires produced the secession of Buenos Aires from the Argentine Confederation with the so-called "September 11 Revolution

[342] The Confederation then formed its own army composed of the National Guards of the provinces, and Buenos Aires did the same

[343] The Argentine Confederation, after the Constitution of 1853 was passed, adopted the republican, representative and federal system as its form of state

[344] The preamble to its Magna Carta indicates as one of the fundamental aspects for the structuring of the State the need to "provide for the common defense", while Article 83 grants the President of the Nation, in his capacity as Head of State, the role of commander of the Armed Forces

[345] Article 22 establishes that "all Argentines are obliged to arm themselves in defense of the Homeland and the Constitution" and defines the powers of the National Congress regarding national defense

[346] THE CONSOLIDATION OF THE STATE (1861 – 1880) The Battle of Pavón, favorable to the Province of Buenos Aires, represented the beginning of the consolidation of the Argentine National State as it is known today, organizing the country according to constitutional guidelines, fully integrating the Province of Buenos Aires into the Republic and nationalizing the Buenos Aires customs

[347] Paraguay's capture of the city of Corrientes led to Argentina's entry into the Triple Alliance War, which it fought alongside Brazil and Uruguay against the former

[348] Due to the demands of that conflict, the government of Bartolomé Mitre, through Law No. 129, declared mandatory enrollment in the active National Guard for all Argentine citizens between seventeen and forty-five years of age, if married, or up to fifty if single

[349] The five years of the Paraguayan War (1865-1870) represented a military experience that prompted the Argentine government to modernize the Armed Forces in line with what was happening in other countries in the region and around the world

[350] Thus, under the presidency of Domingo Faustino Sarmiento (1868-1874) – who had capitalized on the experience of his stay as ambassador in the United States and France – the creations of the National Military College and the Naval Military School were finalized, for the recruitment and training of officers of the land and naval forces

[351] Also notable in those years was the purchase of two monitors and two gunboats, among other vessels, thus bringing together Argentina with a small but modern fleet – which would grow significantly towards the beginning of the 20th century – and also creating the Navy arsenal in Zárate

[352] In 1872, Recruitment Law No. 542 was passed, replacing the provincial law of 1823 and establishing that the Regular Army would be composed of volunteers, recruits, hired and assigned as a penalty, and, in case of insufficient numbers, by national guards from the provinces

[353] The expansion of agricultural exploitation and the persistence of border disputes with other states led to the Argentine State's occupation of territories inhabited by indigenous peoples

[354] With the antecedent of the "Desert Campaign" carried out by Juan Manuel de Rosas between 1833 and 1834, Chapter IV Part II during the government of President Nicolás Avellaneda (1874-1880) the so-called "Conquest of the Desert" was carried out between 1878 and 1879, led by his Minister of War, Julio Argentino Roca, with the occupation of the south of Buenos Aires and La Pampa up to the Negro River and the extreme south of Patagonia

[355] From the same period are the expeditions of Luis Piedrabuena and Luis Py occupying the coasts of the current province of Santa Cruz

[356] Between 1870 and 1879, the Southern and Central Chaco had also been effectively taken possession of in what are now the provinces of Chaco and Formosa

[357] The process of consolidation of the National State ends with the defeat inflicted by the National Army on the military forces of the province of Buenos Aires, which had ignored the election results, led by Governor Carlos Tejedor

[358] As a result, the National Congress approved Law No. 1,072, which prohibited provinces from having military bodies, regardless of their name

[359] Once Julio Argentino Roca was elected president (1880-1886), his Minister of War, Benjamín Victorica, drafted a project that became Law No. 1254 on Military Cadres and Promotions in 1882. This law established the primary bases for the development of the land-based military institution, defining the ranks and reporting periods. Following these guidelines, the reorganization of the General Directorate of the Army was decreed in January 1884, authorizing weapons inspectors to study foreign regulations that could serve as an organizational model

[360] It was during this period that systematic work on developing doctrine began

[361] In 1886, an ad hoc commission studied French, Belgian, and Prussian regulations, opting for the French model, even though the Prussian army was already considered the most modern military instrument of its time

[362] It is worth recalling, in this regard, the military successes of Prussia against Austria-Hungary at Sadowa and against France at Sedan, which demonstrated – among other factors – the superiority of the cadre-conscript troop recruitment system

[363] However, despite the important work carried out, the military profession was not entirely consolidated

[364] A military career was not yet an exclusive activity for members of the Armed Forces, who combined their military duties with political office, agricultural, or commercial activities

[365] Only after the Revolution of 1890, and faced with the possibility of border conflicts, did the State begin an accelerated process of updating

[366] The immediate actions were to purchase state-of-the-art weapons. Federalize the conscription of militias in 1892, and pass Law No. 3190, the first code of military justice

[367] Law No. 3318 on the Organization of the Army and the National Guard established its integration as a permanent army, made up of volunteers, contracted personnel, assigned personnel, and Argentines who had reached the age of twenty in the previous year, who would be called up annually for military service for a period of sixty days and, after this period, transferred to be incorporated into the active National Guard

[368] Although the aforementioned actions represented a notable advance in the process of military modernization, at the beginning of the 20th century, structural changes were still needed to organize an institutionally sound defense system, military education in line with the current technological paradigm, adequate territorial deployment, a stable recruitment system, and objective professionalization of the career

[369] In 1898, with Roca's second term in office and growing tensions with Chile, a greater push was made to modernize the military

[370] A new law on ministries created the Ministries of War and Navy, independent of each other, and for the first time established a separate hierarchy for each of these forces

[371] Colonel Pablo Ricchieri took over as Minister of War under President Roca in July

[372] His extensive European experience, particularly his knowledge of the Prussian and French armies, qualified him to undertake the structural transformation that the Government sought

[373] Law No. 4031 on the Organization of the Army established that military service is mandatory for all Argentine men between the ages of twenty and forty-five, with a six-month recruitment period, except for one-fifth for two years

[374] The adoption of the cadre-conscript system served to modernize the military, while also fulfilling the intended objective of integrating the country's significant immigration status

[375] The law also established, for the first time, a division of the national territory into seven military jurisdictions, each of which was assigned a regional command to which military units would report

[376] At the same time, it was decided to create the necessary infrastructure to adequately support the planned organization

[377] To this end, a plan was designed to build barracks and accommodations throughout the country, a project that involved the purchase of the Campo de Mayo and Campo de los Andes training camps, and the riding camps to provide horses and mules to the various specialties and the construction of Carenero Dike No. 2 located at the Puerto Belgrano Naval Base for Army services (Law No. 4005 of

[378] Simultaneously, in Bahía Blanca, in the south of the Province of Buenos Aires, construction began on the Puerto Belgrano Navy base, a strategic measure that enabled the war fleet to extend into the South Atlantic

[379] The design of the new Army promoted by General Ricchieri also addressed the training of professional and command bodies

[380] Therefore, and in order to ensure training in line with the evolution of the force, it was established in 1905 that the Military College would be the sole source of officer recruitment

[381] Within its scope, the School of Artillery and Engineering application was created, a precursor to the training of military engineers

[382] The creation of the Higher War College in 1900, with a director and a predominantly German teaching staff, was a fundamental element in raising the professional level

[383] By 1905, promotion to the rank of major required passing an exam at this new school, while from 1915 onwards, promotion to the rank of captain required a one-year course

[384] As complementary support in the Army, the School of Class Application (predecessor of the School of Non-commissioned Officers "Sergeant Cabral") and the School of Military Operations (origin of the School of Army Mechanics) were created, intended for the training of non-commissioned officers of the weapons and services respectively

[385] In 1912, the Military Aviation School was created, the embryo of the Air Force

[386] A complex set of political and economic factors, both local and global – political sectors displaced since the first democratic elections that gave victory to Hipólito Yrigoyen in 1916, foreign economic interests and the local effects of the great crisis of '29 – favored that military fractions, initially in the minority, but with undisguised civilian participation, led a coup d'état in 1930 for the first time in the 20th century, inaugurating a series of ruptures in the constitutional order that would last for almost half a century

[387] Specifically, during this period the Armed Forces underwent a profound restructuring to adapt to the lessons of World War II

[388] The creation of the Air Force, the Mechanized Troops, the Parachute Troops and the Marine Infantry allowed the region to acquire cutting-edge military capabilities

[389] In September 1948, Law No. 13234 on the general organization of the Nation for wartime was passed. This law included the regulation of the highest leadership bodies, mobilization and civil defense, and the creation of the Coordination Staff, the predecessor of the current Joint Chiefs of Staff

[390] CREATION OF THE MINISTRY OF DEFENSE AND NATIONAL SECURITY DOCTRINE (1958 to 1983) In 1958 the Ministry of Defense was created, a restructuring based on a modern criterion of civil-military relations that mediated the military insertion in the structure of the State with a civilian figure who, for the first time, stood between the head of State and the commands of the Armed Forces

[391] Although this Ministry of Defense had a predecessor of the same name that operated between 1949 and 1954, it should be clarified that the "State Secretariat of Defense" was established as a planning body, a continuation of the National Postwar Council, and had no precedence over the Armed Forces

[392] As in other Latin American nations, the so-called Cold War had a profound impact on the ideas and structure of the Argentine defense system from the mid-1950s onwards, reaching its greatest development in the courses taught by French officers at the Superior War College

[393] The first expression of this transformation can be identified with the so-called "Conintes Plan" (Plan for Internal State Upheaval) of

[394] In this context, although the National Defense Doctrine (DDN) continued to govern formally—for the purposes of regulating territorial deployment, calculating officer and non-commissioned officer needs, renewing materials, and calculating the budget—the concept of "national defense" fell into disuse, giving way to that of "national security

[395] Thus, within the framework of the National Security Doctrine (NSD), the Armed Forces maintained the hypothesis of permanent war on different fronts

[396] Progressively, the mission of defending the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Nation was losing its contribution to scientific and industrial development. The First World War had highlighted the vulnerability of any country dependent on the import of industrialized goods and clarified that national security was not based solely on the number of cannons or ships that could be available, but also on the capacity to produce and sustain them during a prolonged war

[397] The strategic thinking of the time—influenced by the ideas of the 19th-century German theorist Von der Goltz, who conceived of war as "the sum total of the nation's moral and material resources"—led Argentine rulers to encourage domestic production of basic inputs for the country's economic development

[398] The oil industry, the steel industry and heavy industry in general, as well as cutting-edge technological progress, will find a decisive boost in war preparations, as explained in Chapter XVII

[401] Argentina's participation in the hemispheric security framework led by the United States took precedence externally, while the persecution of internal opposition groups took precedence internally

[402] Its most dramatic expression was the state terrorism implemented after the coup of March 24, 1976, constituting the period of greatest historical degradation of the Armed Forces

[403] The consolidation of a politically autonomous and organizationally fragmented military model between 1930 and 1983 led to the coexistence of independent armed forces with different doctrines, incompatible equipment, and no parameters for joint training and operations

[404] This operational and logistical autonomy was reflected in the military defeat in the Falklands War, where the deficiencies in joint action were evident

[405] Despite the courage displayed by the warring factions, the military failure in the South Atlantic War highlighted the consequences for the Armed Forces of long years of dedication to politics, demonstrating that this resulted in a growing deprofessionalization

[406] The outcome of the war also made clear the errors committed in the conduct of the conflict at the national and military strategic levels

[407] THE DEMOCRATIC RESTORATION AND TRANSFORMATION OF THE DEFENSE SYSTEM (1983 to 2010) This last period began with the assumption of power by President Raúl Alfonsín in December 1983, and brought with it the disappearance of the Commanders-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, the formal hierarchization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the demilitarization of internal security

[408] In 1988, the National Defense Law ended the validity of the doctrines of national security and ideological borders at the doctrinal and organizational levels, delimiting the concept of national defense to the preparation and response to external state military aggression and without jurisdiction in matters of internal security, strengthening the authority of the President of the Nation and the Ministry of Defense to conduct national defense and the Armed Forces, reinforcing the role of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and establishing norms leading to the implementation of a single direction in military leadership

[410] Regarding the crimes of the military dictatorship (1976-1983), the investigation of human rights violations was promoted through the creation of the National Commission on the Disappearance of Persons (CONADEP) and the promotion of the prosecution of members of the Military Juntas

[411] The so-called "Trial of the Juntas" began in October 1984 and a verdict was issued in December 1985, condemning those most responsible, a historic milestone worldwide

[412] A year later, in December 1986, as a result of growing pressure from military sectors and with the aim of declaring the extinction of all criminal proceedings for human rights violations during the dictatorship, the so-called Final Point Law No. 23,492 was passed

[413] However, in April 1987, a military uprising broke out, triggering a series of insubordinations

[414] In June of that same year, the Executive Branch and the parliamentary majorities agreed to pass another law seeking to prevent the continuation of conflicts: the Due Obedience Law. This law considered acts carried out in compliance with superior orders to be non-punishable, and imposed a new restriction on investigations and the determination of responsibility for human rights violations

[416] In parallel, progress was made based on consensus among the main parliamentary sectors

[418] Since the return of democracy, and particularly during the last decade of the 20th century and the first decade of the 21st, a series of events occurred, both internationally and domestically, that led to the dismantling of the central parameters around which Argentine military institutions had been organized

[419] Domestically, although the defeat in the Falklands War led to a transition "through collapse" toward a democratic regime (not negotiated between the outgoing dictatorial authorities and the new constitutional government), the persistence of authoritarian enclaves was evident

[420] This kind of bad blood was exposed in the actions of some military personnel—active or retired—and certain sectors of society who sought to ensure that the transition was as smooth as possible

[421] This resistance reached its peak with the "carapintadas" uprisings in 1987, twice in 1988, and finally in 1990, resulting in the successful repression of the latter, which definitively consolidated the political leadership of the military instrument

[422] On the external level, the end of the Cold War and the emergence of a dynamic of détente, cooperation, and political and economic integration among the states of the region (particularly the Southern Cone) modified the pillars on which relations between their armed forces had been built, particularly since the second half of the twentieth century

[423] The first adaptation of the defense system to these changes was achieved by building a solid political consensus around the concept of defense itself: its relationship to and difference from internal security, the role of the Armed Forces as a Military Instrument of Defense, and the administrative-functional structure of decision-making

[424] The foundations that supported this process within the framework of the rule of law, both and primarily with regard to the civil government or political leadership of defense, as well as the precise delimitation of functions and responsibilities of all members of the system, were embodied in an organic and systemic regulatory framework

[425] The political and social consensus that crystallized in 1983 and has continued to this day was the ultimate foundation for the redefinitions of the National Defense System, based on three key principles: a) the full subordination of the Armed Forces to civilian constitutional authorities; b) the active exercise of defense policy by the civilian government; and c) the organic and functional separation between national defense and internal security

[465] The National Defense Act of 1988 essentially modified the concept of defense prevalent in the previous law issued in October 1966,8 which, imbued with the so-called National Security Doctrine, had established a virtually comprehensive scope of security and was based on the notion of total and permanent conflict characteristic of the Cold War, foreseeing the possibility of an internal ideological enemy

[466] The new law's definition of national defense, on the other hand, limits its conceptual scope to the response to external state military aggression, including preparation for defense during peacetime

[472] Under the new law, such operational management of the Armed Forces is the exclusive power of the President of the Nation and, through his delegation, of the Minister of Defense, who is also responsible for the heads of the strategic operational commands derived from strategic operational planning

[541] Voluntary Military Service Act of 1995 The Voluntary Military Service Act introduced a significant change in the defence system by replacing the previous Compulsory Military Service in force since 1901 as the standard form of troop recruitment

[542] Beyond its strictly military needs, it had the intended objective of being an instrument of geographic cohesion and social and cultural integration of Argentine society at the beginning of the 20th century

[543] Towards the end of this century, the increased training requirements for soldiers resulting from the development of military technology, which led to a significant international trend toward the implementation of voluntary recruitment, plus the country's sociopolitical circumstances, led to the replacement of the troop recruitment system based on compulsory conscription (cadre-conscript system) with one based on the voluntary presentation of aspiring professional soldiers

[544] The Law also enshrines rights to safeguard human dignity for citizens who, in exceptional situations and on a compulsory basis, provide service in the national defense system, such as the principle of conscientious objection, creating the Substitute Social Service; the elimination of anachronistic gender discrimination by establishing Voluntary Military Service as "the service that Argentine men and women perform of their own free will"; and, finally, the possibility of optimizing the national defense system itself through a model of volunteer soldiers, motivated to learn the military profession, thus enabling full utilization of training and instruction for a longer period of time compared to the one-year duration of the previous Compulsory Military Service

[545] The Law established voluntary recruitment as the standard source of troop incorporation in Argentina, replacing compulsory conscription

[546] However, the latter remained in place for those exceptional cases in which the voluntary personnel incorporated was insufficient to cover the needs of national defense, requiring in this case the incorporation for a maximum period of one year of citizens who in the year of service would have reached eighteen years of age, requiring the sanction of a Law of Congress

[547] Among other clarifications, the Law established that citizens incorporated into Voluntary Military Service would be classified as Voluntary Troops; that the number of soldiers and the quota per force would be set annually by the Presidency of the Nation at the proposal of the Ministry of Defense; that said volunteers could perform operational, logistical, and administrative tasks; that the entry age ranges from eighteen to twenty-four years, and that permanence in the Armed Forces as a soldier lasts only until the age of twenty-eight

[548] It also defined the general conditions, benefits, and everything related to military instruction and training for enlisted personnel in tactical, technical, logistical, and administrative activities that those entering the service must receive

[549] Also, for the indicated exceptional cases in which it was essential to resort to compulsory conscription, it provided for conscientious objection and the performance in such a case of a Substitute Social Service, establishing the characteristics of this in the performance of activities of public utility, which may be fulfilled in the performance of tasks of protection and civil defense, health, social or educational services, environmental conservation, improvement of the rural environment and protection of nature

[550] It also determines the institutions and organizations that will coordinate the performance of the Substitute Social Service, establishing the impediments, obligations, and rights of the persons who perform it

[565] This Law, passed in March 1998, established the following objectives: a) the promotion of vocationally motivated military personnel with high theoretical and practical professional training; b) small operational units with efficient logistical support, capable of carrying out prolonged operations that allow for actions in different specialties and geographical areas; c) commands and general staffs trained to permanently conduct operations, conduct studies, planning, and support leadership at the military strategy, operational strategy, and higher tactical levels; d) political, strategic, logistical, and mobilization provisions that allow, in conflict situations, to increase the operational capabilities of the Armed Forces in a short period of time

[566] and e) the determination of budgetary allocations that allow the described objectives to be met

[584] V. 6 National Intelligence Law of 2001 This Law was the first public organic norm relating to the National Intelligence System and the organizations that comprise it

[585] It also defined the scope of intelligence activity with the aim of protecting the individual rights of the country's inhabitants

[586] The law improves the control of intelligence activities by creating the Bicameral Commission for the Oversight of Intelligence Agencies and Activities and also provides for effectiveness controls that include the general guidelines and objectives set by the executive branch, as well as a National Intelligence Plan

[587] He also abolished the National Intelligence Center, assigning the Intelligence Secretariat the direction of the National Intelligence System, the production of national intelligence, the coordination of the development of national strategic intelligence, and the implementation of counterintelligence

[589] Protection of the Rights and Guarantees of the Population Article 4 of the National Intelligence Law provides that intelligence agencies may not: - Carry out repressive tasks, possess compulsory powers, or perform police or criminal investigation functions on their own, except upon specific request of a competent judicial authority in the framework of a specific case under its jurisdiction, or when authorized to do so by law

[590] Obtaining information, producing intelligence, or storing data about individuals solely on the basis of their race, religious faith, private actions, or political opinion, or their adherence to or membership in partisan, social, union, community, cooperative, welfare, cultural, or labor organizations, as well as any lawful activity they carry out in any sphere of action

[591] Influencing in any way the institutional, political, military, police, social, and economic situation of the country, its foreign policy, the internal life of legally constituted political parties, public opinion, individuals, the media, or legal associations or groups of any kind

[592] Reveal or divulge any type of information acquired in the performance of their duties unless there is a court order or dispensation

[593] The National Intelligence Law represented the first step toward establishing the principle of political leadership and joint action by Military Intelligence agencies, which, until its enactment, had an autonomous approach, led almost exclusively by the Armed Forces themselves

[594] This law, consistent with the provisions of the National Defense Law—particularly Article 15—created the National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence, under the Ministry of Defense, for the purpose of producing military intelligence with a joint vision not limited by the individual views of each of the armed forces

[595] also enabling through its performance the exercise of political direction of military intelligence activity

[596] The regulation makes it easier to specify the powers of military intelligence agencies, referring them exclusively to defense and excluding old paradigms that oriented them toward internal security

[597] It is also the first organic law for the entire National Intelligence System, having a public character in contrast to the regulations that preceded it, and perfecting the external legislative oversight already established by the Internal Security Law

[598] In terms of defense, Article 15 establishes the National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence, defining it as the joint body responsible for the development of military strategic intelligence, reporting directly to the Ministry of Defense

[599] Military strategic intelligence is defined as the branch of intelligence concerned with understanding the capabilities and weaknesses of the military potential of countries of interest for understanding international security phenomena, as well as the geographic environment of strategic operational areas determined by military strategic planning

[600] He also specified the powers of the intelligence agencies of the Armed Forces

[601] AA., providing that their intelligence agencies shall be responsible for producing the strategic and operational intelligence and tactical intelligence necessary for the planning and conduct of military operations, as well as specific technical intelligence

[603] For its part, Article 10 establishes the security classifications applicable within the scope of the National Intelligence System, developing and complementing the provisions of Article 16 of Law

[604] It is also worth highlighting the provisions of Article 16 of the decree

[605] Different levels of military intelligence** **Military strategic intelligence:** Level of intelligence that refers to the knowledge of the capabilities and weaknesses of the military potential of countries of interest from the point of view of national defense, as well as the geographic environment of the strategic operational areas determined by military strategic planning

[606] Strategic operational intelligence:** Level of intelligence that refers to the knowledge, at all times, of the capabilities and weaknesses of enemies or opponents, real or potential, specified explicitly and in a timely manner by higher levels of leadership, which are considered to be able to influence the use of one's own means and in the geographic environments of interest for the planning and conduct of military operations

[607] Tactical intelligence:** A level of intelligence that refers to the knowledge of the capabilities and weaknesses of real or potential enemies or opponents, as well as the geographic environment of interest, necessary for the planning and conduct of high- and low-level tactical military operations.
