[621] National Defense encompasses, in its geographical dimension, the continental spaces, the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, and other insular, maritime, and air spaces of the Republic, as well as the Argentine Antarctic sector, within the scope assigned by international standards and treaties signed or to be signed by the Nation, also considering national citizens and assets in third countries, in international waters, and in international airspace

[622] National Law 23.554/1988, National Defense Law, article

[623] The National Defense System is based on two principles that are the product of broad political and social consensus and that have cemented its normative foundations: the civilian governance of defense and the conceptual differentiation of defense and internal security

[624] The logic of the organization and operation of the defense leadership body and the military instrument itself derives from these principles

[625] CIVIL GOVERNMENT OF DEFENSE The civil government of defense is the leadership exercised by the competent constitutional authorities regarding defense policy and its derived military policy

[626] National defense is the “integration and coordinated action of all the forces of the Nation for the solution of those conflicts that require the use of the Armed Forces in a deterrent or effective manner, to confront aggressions of external origin” and its purpose is to “permanently guarantee the sovereignty and independence of the Nation, its territorial integrity and capacity for self-determination, and to protect the life and liberty of its inhabitants.”

[627] For this purpose, Argentina understands aggression of external origin as “the use of armed force by a State against the sovereignty, territorial integrity or political independence of our country, or in any other form that is incompatible with the Charter of the United Nations”

[628] National Law 23.554/1988, National Defense Law, article 2. PEN Decree 727/2006, regulating Law

[629] The full exercise of the government of defense and its military instrument, the Armed Forces, by the legitimately constituted authorities constitutes one of the pillars of the system

[630] Based on this, the national strategic level sets out the guidelines for defense policy and its resulting military policy, along with the relevant parameters for the organization and operation of the military instrument

[631] Civilian defense governance means that the national strategic level effectively assumes its responsibilities and powers for the planning, evaluation, and control of defense activities, encompassing all aspects of management: human resources, training, operations, equipment, logistics, and finance

[632] CONCEPTUAL DIFFERENTIATION BETWEEN NATIONAL DEFENSE AND INTERNAL SECURITY National defense and internal security activities are conceived as two non-delegable responsibilities of the State that, due to their different nature, deserve a specific approach, strictly regulated, and with specialized bodies and instruments

[633] National defense differs from internal security due to the nature of the functions to be exercised and the diversity of the areas in which such exercise must take place

[634] Within the national territory, its jurisdictional waters and its airspace, Argentine law governs, and there is a single coercive order

[635] The activity to be carried out, therefore, consists of preventing crime and, in the event of its commission, subjecting the offender to trial and the application of punishment

[636] This role requires investigative capacity, knowledge of criminal procedure law and substantive criminal law, the application of the minimum necessary force, rationality, gradualness, strict adaptation of means to ends, and protection of life and physical integrity

[637] At the international level, the absence of a single coercive order requires the defense of national heritage against attacks from other States

[638] This may involve the use of significant violence and high-powered weapons to preserve national existence

[639] External military aggression constitutes the greatest risk that a State may be forced to face and, consequently, demands the development of an adequate defense system

[640] “The fundamental decisions regarding defense – from the determination of the threats or risks that will have to be taken into account, the configuration of an autonomous or collective defense (whether through alliances or the integration of a collective security organization), the strategic attitude that the country will have, to the amounts that society will have to invest in its defense and on what and how they will be spent, how and for what the Armed Forces will be designed, what equipment they will have, what capabilities and readiness status they will have, what scope will research, development and production for defense have, what characteristics and organization will have the non-military aspects of defense such as mobilization and civil defense – respond strictly to the decisions adopted by the democratically elected authorities” José Manuel Ugarte in Workshop II of the White Paper on Defense 2010 “Democracy, Civil Leadership and Human Rights”, National University of Rosario, Rosario, June

[641] There are also various public assets that must be protected: first and foremost are the rights and freedoms that all inhabitants of the country have as such and that must be guaranteed by the political system

[642] And in the second, the very existence of the Nation, its integrity and survival

[643] The rights and freedoms of all inhabitants are the subject of internal security, while the integrity and survival of the Nation are the subject of defense

[644] This difference in objectives entails the need for specific policies and instruments for each one

[645] From this principle derives the functional and operational specialization of State agencies in the areas of Defense, on the one hand, and Internal Security, on the other

[646] Since the restoration of the rule of law in 1983, the need to differentiate between the spheres of Defense and Internal Security has been progressively consolidated in a new body of regulations, the product of widespread political and social consensus

[647] The National Constitution, in its Preamble, already establishes two separate purposes: those relating to “internal peace” and “common defense”

[648] Law 23.554 on National Defense (passed in 1988) and Law 24.059 on Internal Security (passed in 1992) interpret these constitutional principles and unequivocally establish the objectives to which each of the respective systems is focused

[649] The defense, to ward off aggressions of external origin perpetrated by armed forces belonging to one or more other States; while the Internal Security focuses on preserving or restoring, through various instruments of its own, including police institutions and security forces, "the de facto situation based on the law in which the freedom, life and property of the inhabitants, their rights and guarantees and the full validity of the institutions of the representative, republican and federal system established by the National Constitution are protected

[650] National Defense Law, article

[651] Internal Security Law, articles 1, 2 and

[652] The President of the Nation, Cristina Fernández, visits the Argentine Mission in Haiti as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces

[653] The Argentine State's differentiation of both responsibilities does not ignore the complex dynamics of transnational criminal phenomena and the potential overlap between defense and security issues. Rather, it provides for the possibility of an orderly complementarity between the two systems within its legal and institutional framework

[654] This separation generally implies the exclusion of the Armed Forces from matters of internal security, except for the collaboration they may provide in specific and exceptional cases established in the Internal Security Law

[655] In this way, the legislation professionally focuses each of the State agencies on their corresponding missions and functions

[656] The Argentine Republic has specialized institutions to address issues of national defense and internal security in a differentiated manner: the Armed Forces for the former, and the police institutions and security forces for the latter (National Gendarmerie, Argentine Naval Prefecture, Airport Security Police, Argentine Federal Police, and provincial police forces

[657] While the Defense System's mission is to repel military aggression from other States, the Internal Security System's primary purpose is the prevention and prosecution of crimes contained in the Penal Code and other special laws

[658] This difference in the phenomena to be addressed implies specific training, equipment and employment doctrines

[659] Phenomena such as drug trafficking, organized crime, economic crimes, money laundering, and transnational terrorism do not fall within the responsibilities, powers, and instruments of the Argentine Defense System under the Argentine legal and institutional framework

[660] Addressing these criminal phenomena is the responsibility of the Internal Security System through specific police, security, and intelligence agencies and bodies, in accordance with current legislation

[661] “In some countries, defense innovations have been reactive

[662] Growing public insecurity and organized crime that challenge police response capacity quickly led to the involvement of the military in public security

[663] No changes in doctrine, training, or equipment

[664] From one day to the next, we went out onto the streets and, with the urgency of social demand, tried in vain to repair the State's deficits in other areas" Rut Diamint at the 2010 National Seminar on the White Paper on Defense

[665] PURPOSE OF THE DEFENSE SYSTEM The purpose of the National Defense System is: a) to formulate plans that will contribute to the preparation of the Nation for a possible armed conflict and to the conduct of national defense at the different levels corresponding to the military strategy and the operational strategy; b) to attend, from the level of national strategy, to the direction of the war in all its aspects; c) to guide the Armed Forces and the efforts of the sectors of the country affected by the armed conflict at the strategic military and operational levels; d) to prepare and execute national mobilization measures; e) to ensure the execution of joint military operations of the Armed Forces and, eventually, combined operations – those carried out between two or more countries – that may materialize; f) to establish the confluences that will allow for the preparation of the necessary alliances sufficient to conveniently resolve the possible concretion of a war, as well as to control post-war actions

[666] The National Defense System is oriented, both structurally, organizationally, and functionally, toward determining and maintaining the National Defense Policy aimed at warding off external military aggression perpetrated by other States

[667] Any matter related to or related to internal security, responsibilities that fall under the jurisdiction of other State agencies organized and trained for this purpose, are outside its jurisdiction in matters of doctrine, planning, training, and intelligence production

[675] POWERS OF THE MEMBERS OF THE DEFENSE SYSTEM

[676] The President of the Nation is the highest authority of the National Defense System and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces

[677] The President is responsible for the direction of national defense and the leadership of the Armed Forces

[678] powers conferred upon it by the National Constitution

[679] It provides, with the advice of the National Defense Council (CODENA), the content and guidelines for the implementation of national defense planning, controlling its design and execution

[680] As Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, he is responsible for the comprehensive conduct of the war with the advice and assistance of CODENA, and the military conduct of the war with the assistance and advice of the Minister of Defense, the Chief of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Chiefs of the General Staffs of each of the Armed Forces

[681] formed into a “Crisis Committee”

[682] CONGRESS OF THE NATION The main prerogatives of the National Congress are: to authorize the Executive Branch to declare war or make peace; to empower the Executive Branch to order reprisals; to establish the Armed Forces in times of peace and war, and to dictate the rules for their organization and government; to permit the introduction of foreign troops into the territory of the Nation and the withdrawal of national forces from it

[683] In the event of an external attack, it is the exclusive prerogative of the Senate of the Nation to authorize the President of the Republic to declare a state of siege in the Republic

[684] It also approves, through its Agreements Committee, promotions to the rank of senior officers in the Armed Forces

[685] For its part, the Chamber of Deputies is exclusively responsible for initiating laws on contributions and troop recruitment

[686] Parliamentary participation in the Defense System is also exercised through the request for reports from the National Executive Branch

[687] President Néstor Kirchner inspecting Army personnel

[688] The National Defense Council, as an integral part of the Defense System, is chaired by the President of the Nation and comprised of the Vice President of the Nation; the ministers of the National Cabinet; the head of the highest-level national intelligence agency; the presidents of the Defense Committees of the Senate and the Chamber of Deputies of the Nation, and two members of said committees, one from the majority bloc and the other from the largest minority bloc; and, when the Minister of Defense deems it necessary, the Chief of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Chiefs of the General Staffs of each of the Armed Forces may also be convened

[689] The National Defense Council's mission is to assist and advise the President of the Nation in determining conflicts and preparing plans and coordinating the actions necessary for their resolution

[690] It is responsible for assisting and advising the President on matters related to determining the basic guidelines of the National Defense Policy, through the design and preparation of periodic and special reports, evaluations, opinions, or projects to identify risk situations that may affect national sovereignty and independence

[691] It is also responsible for preparing comprehensive diagnoses of the national strategic situation, specifying and describing actors, situations, and trends that are of interest to national defense, whether at the regional or global levels

[692] These documents seek to identify areas or spheres of common interest for the development and design of projects or proposals for joint work with the various departments of the State on matters related to national defense that, given their nature, require an interdisciplinary approach from the National State

[693] Within the framework of these working procedures, the final preparation of these documents is the responsibility of the Ministry of Defense, which acts as Executive Secretariat of CODENA

[695] The Ministry of Defense is responsible for the direction, organization, and coordination of activities related to national defense that are not reserved or carried out directly by the President of the Nation, or that are not assigned by law to another official, body, or organization

[696] The Ministry of Defense, through its participation in CODENA, assists and advises the President of the Nation in the overall conduct of the war and, in turn, in the military conduct of the war

[697] It is responsible for developing and conducting defense and military policy, particularly with regard to the organization, operation, deployment, human resources, infrastructure, logistics, materiel, information, training, and doctrine of the military instrument

[698] The Ministry also establishes the qualifications required to hold the positions of Chief of the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces and Chief of the General Staffs of each of the Armed Forces

[699] The Ministry of Defense is also responsible for developing the principles, rules, or fundamental guidelines that must govern the exercise of the functions conferred on the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces, approving Military Strategic Planning, and adapting the organic and functional structures of the Armed Forces

[700] and the creation of new operational units

[701] Likewise, the Ministry of Defense is responsible for formulating and submitting to the President of the Nation proposals for promotion, continued rank, retirement, or discharge of senior military personnel (officers) from the Armed Forces, following an evaluation of their background, qualifications, and professional performance

[702] It is also a ministerial responsibility to submit to the President of the Nation the evaluation of the background, qualifications, and professional performance of those members of the Armed Forces who meet the requirements to occupy the positions of Chief of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces or Chief of the General Staffs of each of the Armed Forces

[703] As a specific clarification of ministerial powers and responsibilities, the general regulatory framework of State also establishes that the war powers of the President of the Nation (in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces) and his constitutional powers in this area will correspond to the office of the Minister of Defense

[704] Other ministerial powers specified in the Argentine regulatory framework are as follows: Political responsibility, as an organ of the National Executive Branch, for the organization and operation of the Defense System and its component agencies

[705] Responsibility in the senior management of the operation and general organization of the Armed Forces, the execution of the Defense Planning Cycle and the implementation of the corresponding military policy

[706] Responsibility for the systemic and comprehensive management of national defense resources, maximizing efficiency in their use, and achieving effective joint military action

[707] Responsibility for the military instrument to adopt the organizational and functional forms required by military strategic planning or by decisions issued by the National Executive Branch

[802] This is conceived as an integrative body of the three operational environments, and its composition, size, and deployment are derived from strategic defense planning

[803] Its structure must be guided by criteria of organization and joint efficiency, seeking the unification of functions, activities and services whose nature is not specific to a single force

[804] The Armed Forces are dedicated exclusively to enlisting, training, and maintaining the human resources and material means placed at their disposal

[805] This means that force redesign criteria, geographic redeployment initiatives, personnel structure modifications, or decisions to incorporate or decommission weapons systems are reserved for strategic defense planning, which is formulated by the Joint Chiefs of Staff and evaluated and approved by the Ministry of Defense

[806] CONCEPT OF THE MILITARY INSTRUMENT AND CONDITIONS FOR ITS EFFECTIVE USE National defense conceives the Armed Forces as organizations articulated around joint military action

[807] Therefore, a military instrument is only suitable and effective for fulfilling its mission if it is conceived, planned, and operated as an integrated instrument, assuming joint action even in cases involving only one force

[808] This joint nature of the military instrument extends to all facets of the organization and operation of the Armed Forces

[809] doctrine, planning, force design, formation, training, operations and logistics

[810] Joint military action is understood as the planning and coordinated use of all the means and resources available to each armed force to achieve specific objectives through comprehensive operational management

[811] The concept of a military instrument implies the efficient use of military resources, the integrated employment of forces, the consolidation of operational capabilities, and the comprehensive management and functional control of the entire system to fulfill its primary and subsidiary missions

[812] This approach involves the joint formulation of doctrine, planning, and operation of all components of the military instrument under the unified authority of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (EMCO) and the approval and supervision of the Ministry of Defense

[813] In strictly military terms, the conception of the military instrument, especially its conduct and conditions of employment, is based on the principles of joint military action: JOINT MILITARY DOCTRINE An organic set of essential concepts, principles, criteria, and terms that guide the preparation and employment of the military instrument, both in times of peace and war; and that contribute to the fulfillment of its mission within the framework of joint military action

[814] Its formulation and updating is the responsibility of a Doctrine Committee led by the Ministry of Defense and composed of the highest doctrinal authorities of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Armed Forces

[815] JOINT MILITARY STRATEGIC PLANNING Phase of defense planning that, based on national strategic level guidelines, aims to determine the capabilities and subsystems of the military instrument, namely: human resources, infrastructure, logistics, material, information, training, organization and doctrine

[816] This dynamic and permanent process is described in chapter XV

[817] JOINT TRAINING** Activities to incorporate skills and abilities developed by the Armed Forces for their personnel in order to increase capabilities for joint military action

[818] d. **UNITY OF COMMAND** Use of the military instrument through the exercise of leadership under a single command, in order to ensure unity of effort, economy of resources and maximum coordination in the fulfillment of the mission

[819] e. **MAXIMUM INTEGRATION** Pursuit of the greatest possible interoperability and complementarity between the Armed Forces, at their different levels and throughout their entire organic-functional structure

[820] The goal is to achieve harmonious action, economy of resources, and maximum performance within a context that considers unity of purpose and the specific nature of each Force. f. **FULL UTILIZATION OF FORCES** Maximum employment and exploitation of the comprehensive capabilities of the military instrument

[821] All these principles are based on the assumption that the effective use of military instruments requires the comprehensive design, control, and management of all the means and resources available within the military system, regardless of its configuration (operational units, task forces, joint components, strategic commands, etc

[822] The main mission of the military instrument of defense is to ward off and repel all external aggression of military-state origin, in order to permanently safeguard the vital interests of the Nation: sovereignty, independence, self-determination, territorial integrity, and the life and liberty of its inhabitants

[823] In this way, the Armed Forces are doctrinally, organically, functionally and materially structured based on their primary mission

[824] This goal is the guiding criterion for force design, as subsidiary missions should not affect the capabilities required to fulfill their primary mission

[825] SUBSIDIARY MISSIONS The subsidiary missions of the military instrument are: United Nations multilateral operations. Internal security operations provided for by the Internal Security Law. Operations in support of the national community or friendly countries. Participation of the Armed Forces

[826] in the construction of a subregional defense system

[827] The fulfillment of subsidiary missions must not compromise the capabilities of the military instrument to effectively fulfill its primary mission

[828] Some clarifications are in order regarding these missions

[829] First, regarding the role of the Armed Forces in United Nations multilateral operations, such participation must be considered in strictly technical-military terms and as an intervening variable in the design, determination, and updating of the military instrument's capabilities, particularly with regard to achieving the standards required for multilateral military interaction

[830] Of course, this participation should not compromise the resources and capabilities required to fulfill the military instrument's primary mission

[831] Secondly, the participation of the Armed Forces in the construction of a subregional defense system based on the progressive consolidation of greater levels of mutual trust must be considered a key factor in the design and determination of the military instrument's capabilities

[832] This criterion must be specifically considered with regard to achieving levels of interoperability with the countries of the subregion, in order to reach the desired standards in terms of joint and combined action

[833] Thirdly, with regard to operations to support the national community or friendly countries in the event of disasters or other circumstances provided for in the regulations, it is considered that these will be carried out using the remaining operational and logistical capabilities of the Armed Forces

[834] This is because, although such operations are considered important, they cannot and should not interfere with the fulfillment of the primary mission of the military instrument

[835] Finally, and in accordance with the provisions of Internal Security Law No. 24,059, it should be noted that the Argentine Armed Forces may carry out actions to guarantee internal security only within the strict limits detailed in Chapter V, Section

[840] PRIORITIZATION OF CAPABILITIES OF THE MILITARY INSTRUMENT AND ITS EQUIPMENT In line with Argentina's defensive strategic conception, positioning and attitude, the prioritization of capabilities of the military instrument is guided, first and foremost, by the objective of guaranteeing effectiveness in the fulfillment of the main mission

[841] The second is guided by the fulfillment of the responsibilities of subsidiary missions that refer to multilateral military interaction

[842] Based on the established priorities, strategic planning is guided by the following parameters: - That the capabilities correspond to the profile, nature and defensive strategic attitude of the military instrument

[843] That these capabilities promote and consolidate integration and coordinated action among the operational elements of the three Armed Forces

[844] That capabilities ensure the effective complementation of the integration of the military instrument and avoid the overlapping of capabilities, means, and resources

[845] That the capacities are feasible and acceptable in budgetary terms

[846] The above criteria correspond to a media-derived “profile” that conforms to the following guidelines: **MAIN MISSION** **SUBSIDIARY MISSIONS** UN Operations Construction of a subregional defense system Community support Support for Internal Security Uses surplus resources

[847] It does not influence the design of forces, doctrine and means

[848] It influences the design of forces, doctrine and means

[849] Ward off and repel military aggression from other States Missions of the National Defense System

[850] Operational correspondence with the design formulated for the military instrument. - Prioritization of the criteria of multi-skilling, versatility, and operational flexibility

[851] This involves means that allow for the fulfillment and development of various tasks within the framework of the assigned missions

[852] Prioritization of standardization and homogenization processes for materials and equipment used in different weapons systems

[853] Standardization of existing material resources, both at a specific and aggregate level

[854] Prioritization of recovery, modernization, or equipment acquisition programs that allow for new developments and domestic production or that involve significant technology transfer

[855] Once the direction guiding the prioritization of the military instrument's operational capabilities has been considered—in the order detailed below—the alternatives for recovery, modernization, or incorporation of material

[856] This determination is made on the basis of the criteria of suitability, feasibility and acceptability

[857] Briefly: - The recovery of decommissioned material, when feasible and acceptable, and provided that it remains capable of meeting the necessary operational capabilities

[858] The modernization of available material, when this is suitable, feasible and acceptable to meet the planned operational capabilities

[859] The incorporation of new material in cases where priority is given to equipment and systems that provide new developments, with the transfer of the technology involved and the equipment necessary for simulated operational training

[860] Ultimately, the Ministry of Defense decides between different alternatives based on the capabilities to be achieved by the military instrument, taking into consideration the profile of the equipment that must contribute to those capabilities and the guidelines that must be followed for the alternatives for its recovery, modernization, or incorporation

[861] In this process, the political leadership is advised by the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces (EMCO), which determines the suitability of the means in question

[865] The Foreign Security Cabinet, for the purposes of preparing and conducting war and for greater coordination of the Armed Forces in joint operations, will be permanently assisted by the Coordination Staff, which will be directly subordinate to and will be integrated with Chiefs and Officers of the General Staffs of the Army, Navy and Air Force, in accordance with the organization, objectives and powers that the National Defense Council establishes when regulating its activities

[874] JOINT MILITARY ACTION As described in the previous section, although the concept of “jointness” is not new to the Argentine Armed Forces, “joint action” itself was not really applied until after the conflict over the Malvinas Islands in

[875] From this experience, the failure of which largely stemmed from the lack of integration and coordination among the various military components, this criterion began to materialize, consequently increasing the responsibilities of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces

[876] Joint military action consists of the coherent, coordinated, and systematic development, design, use, and execution of measures, provisions, and activities using the means and resources made available by two or more Armed Forces, under a single command and with the same purpose, during all stages of military operations: planning, preparation, use, and execution of activities

[877] Although each Armed Force has its own resources to fulfill its specific functions, joint action reinforces and complements their capabilities, granting them greater power, flexibility, mobility, and speed, thus achieving a combined operational level greater than the sum of their individual capabilities

[878] Thus, the suitability, effectiveness and efficiency of the military instrument to fulfill its mission requires that it be conceived, planned and used as an integrated instrument, which is why military action is necessarily understood as joint action

[879] The Joint Staff of the Armed Forces (EMCO) is the highest military authority providing assistance and advice to the Minister of Defense on military strategic matters and the body responsible for conducting peacetime operations, whether specific, joint or combined

[880] It is responsible for the formulation of joint doctrine, the development of joint military planning, the direction of joint military training, and the supervision and control of operational strategic planning

[881] Personnel from the Argentine Army, Navy and Air Force carrying out the joint exercise “H-20”, developed on November 12, 2008 in the surroundings of the City of Goya, Province of Corrientes

[882] The EMCO is the body responsible for the use of military means in peacetime and, to this end, exercises functional control over the General Staffs of each of the Armed Forces and operational control over their elements

[883] As a result, the Armed Forces

[884] They have the mission of preparing, training and maintaining the means at their disposal

[885] The Chief of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces is appointed from among the active generals, admirals, or brigadiers of the command corps. He holds the highest military rank, exercising superiority by position over the rest of the military personnel of the Armed Forces

[886] For the purposes of this designation, the Ministry of Defense is the body that determines the professional qualifications required to hold this position, detailing the necessary and exclusive requirements in terms of training, qualifications, and professional performance

[887] The EMCO is made up of personnel from the three Armed Forces based on their needs and requirements

[888] Joint military action is the cornerstone of the Armed Forces' modernization process, as it is the key to the effective implementation of the military instrument

[889] In this framework, the EMCO stands as the competent body for the comprehensive and functional management of the “military system”

[890] To this end, it has, for peacetime operations, the attribution of functional and operational control over all military means and resources that comprise the National Defense System, regardless of the configuration adopted by these means and resources (operational units, task forces, joint components or strategic commands

[891] To fulfill its mission, the EMCO develops military strategic planning, develops joint and joint-combined doctrine, directs and controls joint training, and operationally manages the nation's military instrument in peacetime

[892] All of this is in pursuit of the efficient use of military resources, the integrated employment of the Armed Forces, the consolidation of operational capabilities, and the comprehensive management and functional control of the entire military system

[893] Within the framework of these responsibilities, the EMCO has powers to integrate and standardize the set of rules and procedures relating to the employment of military assets, with the aim of achieving their efficient use

[894] For the purpose of fulfilling his operational responsibilities in peacetime, the head of the EMCO has a single, permanent subordinate authority: the Joint Operational Command

[895] THE JOINT OPERATIONAL COMMAND It is the unified military body, of a joint and permanent nature, responsible in times of peace for the direction and coordination of military operations

[896] The head of this operational command, with the rank of general, admiral, or brigadier of the active command corps, is appointed by the President of the Nation at the proposal of the Minister of Defense

[897] The Joint Operational Command is the body responsible for carrying out joint military training, controlling joint exercises, developing and executing strategic operational planning and military operations, and consequently exercising operational command over the resources that may eventually be at its disposal, since it lacks organic operational forces, which, once required, will be provided by the General Staffs of each of the Nation's Armed Forces

[898] The importance of this operational instance of the military instrument is reflected in its functions: - Plan, conduct, coordinate, supervise and intervene in the operations carried out by the Armed Forces in peacetime

[899] Advise and assist the head of the EMCO on operational strategy and military and operational strategic planning

[900] Understand the execution of joint military training and participate in the formulation and updating of joint and combined military doctrine

[901] Conduct and supervise the activities carried out by the Joint Antarctic Command

[902] Exercise functional control over the various joint commands to carry out the missions assigned to it

[903] Propose the incorporation of means outside the Armed Forces

[906] Part II THE ARMED FORCES Chapter IX The land, naval and air components of the military instrument have specific characteristics in accordance with the environment for which they prepare, train and maintain their personnel and operational means

[907] THE ARMED FORCES

[908] THE ARGENTINE ARMY The breadth and diversity of the land areas of Argentina have exerted a decisive influence on the development of the Army, both in terms of deployment and magnitude and operational qualities

[909] For this reason, the land component of the military instrument is conceived according to three types of military force: a) Regional response forces, whose deployments and organization are based on the need to have troops specially trained to fight in the geographical environments of the mountains, hills and Patagonian steppe

[910] The main defense forces, structured on the basis of medium and heavy organizations

[911] Rapid intervention forces, with light and eventually medium-sized organizations

[912] ARGENTINE NAVY Just as with land spaces, maritime areas under national jurisdiction are of enormous proportions

[913] Added to this is an extensive river network that constitutes an important communication route within the continent

[914] This has created a historic need to operate in the maritime, river, and island operational spheres with an adequate deployment of support bases, both for the technical support of naval units and for coastal surveillance for national defense purposes

[915] Personnel of the 601 Assault Helicopter Battalion based in Campo de Mayo conducting training exercises

[916] Argentine Army VC TAM tank fording a watercourse

[917] The size of the areas involved and the importance of maritime and river routes for international trade, regional productive development and communications in general, highlight the need to have naval forces with sufficient operational capabilities to adequately fulfill the role of naval component of the military instrument

[918] Through the National Maritime Search and Rescue Agency (SAR, the international acronym for Search and Rescue), the Navy fulfills its responsibilities to safeguard human life at sea within the framework of the 1979 Hamburg SAR Convention of the International Maritime Organization

[919] ARGENTINE AIR FORCE The intangibility of airspace, its dimensions from the Earth's surface to outer space and the dynamics that develop and project onto it generate an undeniable impact on matters of National Defense

[920] This raises the need for permanent strategic surveillance and control—in the dual dimension of use and denial of three-dimensional space—based on an effective aerospace defense system, as determined by joint military planning

[921] The deployment, readiness conditions, technological and operational quality of the resources, and the control capacity of the spaces—including the satellite segment—determine the level of capability the system requires to meet the employment forecasts outlined in the aforementioned planning

[922] The design of the aerospace component of the military instrument, within the framework of adequate operational, logistical, and technological performance, must consider: the capacity for networked and real-time planning; the integration of surveillance and control systems from the various operational areas in the areas of interest; joint and combined interoperability standards; the flexibility to modify the defensive axis; and precision in engagement

[923] In 2010, the Ministry of Defense approved a common matrix for the organic-functional structure of the Armed Forces with the aim of standardizing it in accordance with the functions of readiness, training and maintenance of means, based on the criteria of operational integration and joint military action

[924] Consequently, the organization of the three Armed Forces has a common structure

[926] Part II Chapter IX of senior leadership, headed by the Chief of the General Staff, which includes a support structure, reporting to the Deputy Chief of the General Staff, and a Readiness and Training Command on which the operational units depend

[927] The Readiness and Training Commands are tasked with planning and conducting the readiness and training of operational and support assets within the framework determined by joint military planning

[928] The common support structure for the three forces includes the areas of organization and doctrine; research and development; materiel; intelligence; education; health; personnel and welfare; and communications and information technology

[929] Argentine Army The Army Training and Readiness Command is made up of three Army divisions (large battle units) which are in turn made up of brigades (large combat units) and formations

[930] The brigades respond to the concept of a weapons system

[931] Its units complement each other in their functions with the aim of gaining operational autonomy

[932] It is the smallest unit with independent “inter-arms” combat capability

[933] In addition to their specific characteristics, all have the corresponding fire support, combat support and logistics means

[934] The different types of brigade are: Armored brigades: formed on the basis of three tank cavalry regiments and one mechanized infantry regiment

[935] Their crew vehicles are designed for combat against armored units

[936] Mechanized brigades: composed of two mechanized infantry regiments and one tank cavalry regiment

[937] These brigades have various types of tracked mechanized armored vehicles, suitable for infantry combat, ground reconnaissance, and combat against mechanized units

[938] Mountain and hill brigades: made up of two or more mountain or hill infantry and cavalry regiments

[939] In the case of mountain brigades, units are equipped with lightweight materials that are easily transportable on mules and horses

[940] Part II Chapter IX Submarine TR-1700 of the Argentine Navy

[941] Flotilla of the Argentine Navy

[942] Part II Chapter IX - Paratrooper Brigade: its structure is based on two paratrooper regiments

[943] Its material and equipment are designed to be transported, unloaded and eventually launched from aircraft in flight

[944] All personnel are qualified to parachute directly into the area of military operations

[945] The Training and Readiness Command also has a Rapid Deployment Force

[946] Its structure is made up of light elements (air assault, paratroopers, commandos) and eventually medium elements (wheeled vehicles

[947] It has the capacity to project resources to respond immediately to a crisis situation

[948] Argentinian Navy The Navy Training and Readiness Command is composed of two types of groups: the force commands for the different operational environments (sea fleet, naval aviation, marine infantry and submarines) and the naval areas

[949] Force commands manage the forces and units under their command: surface ships, submarines, aircraft, and marine infantry units

[950] Its purpose is to be able to provide and sustain the resources required for operational naval training, the composition of the required joint or joint-combined forces, and the operations with naval resources carried out by the EMCO Operational Command

[951] Naval areas are responsible for providing logistical support—through their bases—to operational assets based within their jurisdiction or conducting operations in their area of responsibility

[952] Some of them have permanently assigned resources appropriate for the area

[953] Naval Fleet Command: Responsible for integrated naval training

[954] It also has attached naval and air infantry units

[955] It is composed of: - A division of destroyers for anti-surface, anti-submarine, anti-missile defense and electronic warfare actions

[956] A division of corvettes for sea control tasks and for anti-surface, anti-submarine, missile defense, and electronic warfare actions

[957] The Naval Amphibious and Logistics Command, responsible for planning and executing amphibious exercises, anti-aircraft defense tasks, and logistical support for the Naval Fleet

[1000] ARGENTINE ARMY The Army's tactical units are equipped with material means for the various functions in the field of operations: - for close combat, the infantry and cavalry organizations; - for fire support, the field artillery and anti-aircraft artillery organizations; - for combat support, the engineering, communications, intelligence, and Army aviation organizations; - for logistical support, the combat support services (arsenals, quartermaster, health, veterinary, justice, among others

[1001] To act directly, most organizations are equipped with various types of mechanized and armored combat vehicles, personnel carriers, and rotary-wing or fixed-wing aircraft that operate closely with ground units

[1002] Organizations designed to operate in mountains and hills are equipped with lightweight equipment similar to that of airborne units

[1003] Fire support resources, for their part, are incorporated into field artillery or anti-aircraft artillery organizations

[1004] The material resources available to organizations dedicated to combat support respond to the need to facilitate their own mobility in that field and, at the same time, restrict that of the adversary

[1005] It also seeks to guarantee the command and control of operations through the use of communication media

[1006] There is also combat intelligence equipment, combat support service units with the means to fulfill the functions of supplying, maintaining, and transporting materiel, and providing healthcare to combatants

[1041] The Argentine military also carries out operations outside the country, within the framework of the agreements and obligations assumed by the State for participation in United Nations peacekeeping missions, and for humanitarian assistance and support to communities in friendly countries

[1043] X. 1 150 Part II Chapter X X. 1 NATIONAL AIRSPACE SURVEILLANCE AND RECONNAISSANCE OPERATIONS

[1044] Argentina has launched the National Aerospace Surveillance and Control System (SINVICA

[1045] Its purpose is to control movements in airspace under national jurisdiction, including those originating from or heading towards third countries, carrying out aerospace defense and air traffic control tasks

[1046] In addition, in February 2007 the Ministry of Defense implemented "actions contributing to the strengthening of surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities" to increase, in the first instance, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities in the "northeast" and "northwest" air defense zones

[1047] Until then, surveillance and reconnaissance were carried out solely by Air Force means

[1048] The mobile radars installed since 2004, belonging to the Air Force, were later joined by mobile radars from the Army, which allowed for increased surveillance and control capabilities

[1049] While airspace surveillance is a national defense task carried out by the Air Force, it also constitutes an activity that potentially supports the justice system and security forces in search and rescue operations in air disasters and the detection of irregular and illegal flights

[1050] Therefore, in June 2007, the deployment of the necessary resources to form the Joint Task Force for Aerospace Control "Fortín" began

[1051] This joint task force is composed of Air Force and Army radars deployed in the north of the country, in the so-called Northeast Air Defense Zone (ZODANE), and Air Force assets deployed at their bases to detect suspected irregular air traffic

[1052] All of this is carried out under the operational control of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces (EMCO), through its Operational Command

[1053] The information provided by the sensors deployed on the ZODANE is received in real time at the Merlo Aerospace Surveillance Center (CVAM), from where operations aimed at intercepting and identifying aircraft whose activity is not properly recorded are directly commanded

[1054] The “Fortín” task force also receives collaboration from the Federative Republic of Brazil

[1055] This country provides information obtained through its own surveillance radars, within the framework of ongoing cooperation between the air forces of Brazil and Argentina, which includes the periodic implementation of exercises known as “Plata”

[1056] These tasks are complemented by the incorporation of a team loaned by the Kingdom of Spain, called AN/FPS-113 AN/FPS-90, in the city of Resistencia (Chaco province), inaugurated in October

[1057] The incorporation of this equipment constitutes another step in the National Radarization Plan, which will be completed with the incorporation of the Argentine Primary Radar manufactured by INVAP, a state-owned company dedicated to the design and construction of complex technological systems

[1058] This type of military radar will represent Argentina's access to a technological threshold mastered by very few countries

[1059] The push for manufacturing will provide technological independence and open up the future possibility of selling high-value-added items worldwide

[1060] DEPLOYMENT IN DEFENSE ZONES: PROTECTION OF PRESIDENTIAL SUMMITS Another of the activities assigned to the military instrument from the highest national leadership is the protection of presidential summits

[1061] Within this framework, the Argentine defense system—through the Joint Chiefs of Staff—planned and executed aerospace defense measures in conjunction with the holding of presidential summits on national territory

[1062] Among others: 1- IV Summit of the Americas (Mar del Plata, November 2005): deployment of three Mirage III, three A4-AR, three IA-58 Pucará, one P-3 Orion aircraft, one Bell-212, one mobile radar, the Destroyer ARA Sarandí, the Corvettes ARA Drummond and ARA Guerrico, the Avisos ARA Suboficial Castillo and ARA Gurruchaga

[1063] th Mercosur Summit (Córdoba, July 2006): deployment of two A4-AR, three IA-58 Pucará, one Bell-212 and one mobile radar

[1064] The data on irregular air traffic (TAI) obtained in the surveillance operations of the national airspace is transferred to the Secretariat of Programming for the Prevention of Drug Addiction and the Fight against Drug Trafficking (SEDRONAR), which allows this agency to have access to information on detections of unidentified aircraft, as well as any additional data obtained for the purpose of combating illegal drug trafficking

[1065] The detection of air traffic that cannot be recognized through regular channels makes it necessary to identify it through standardized interception procedures

[1066] Once this phase is completed, and it is confirmed that the flight is stealthy, the information is transferred in real time to the Secretariat of Internal Security so that it can take the necessary measures to arrest the suspect by the appropriate security or police forces

[1067] On April 19, 2007, an agreement was established between the Secretariat for Programming for the Prevention of Drug Addiction and the Fight against Drug Trafficking of Argentina (SEDRONAR) and the Ministry of Defense, in accordance with the provisions of Decree PEN 727/06 regulating the National Defense Law

[1068] AN-FPS 113/AN-FPS 90 radar located in the city of Resistencia, Chaco

[1077] SEA CONTROL AND MARITIME PATROL OPERATIONS Regarding sea control and maritime patrol, the Operational Command has resources provided by the Argentine Navy assigned in two Naval Areas to carry out these tasks

[1078] The Atlantic Naval Area's main task is to optimize sea control functions and is responsible for all matters relating to maritime interests

[1079] The Mar del Plata Naval Base is the natural base of the area, whose operational jurisdiction extends from Punta Indio (Buenos Aires Province) to the city of Comodoro Rivadavia, with more than 2,500 km of coastline and an area equivalent to one million square kilometers of the Argentine Sea

[1080] For these tasks, the ARA has six surface vessels, three A-69 Corvettes, and three ATF-type Avisos, which make up the organic units of the Maritime Patrol Division Command (DVPM

[1081] This division works in coordination with the Naval Air Surveillance and Exploration Squadrons, which have B-200 Cormorant and P-3B Orion aircraft systems (permanently based at the Almirante Zar Naval Air Base in the city of Trelew), linked in flight with the Atlantic Naval Area Operations Center and the units at sea, maintaining close surveillance

[1082] Navy personnel engaged in maritime patrol duties

[1084] surveillance of fishing vessels of different flags operating near mile marker

[1085] The Southern Naval Area extends from the southern tip of continental Argentina, the Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego and Isla de los Estados, and includes the vast southern maritime spaces up to the 60th parallel south, with its natural seat being the city of Ushuaia

[1086] This Area is responsible for carrying out tasks related to the search and rescue of vessels in emergency situations on the high seas, the control of the sea and its resources, and the custody of the Beagle Channel

[1087] To this end, the Southern Naval Area Command has a Fast Boat Group consisting of six vessels

[1088] During the summer months, Operation Shield is implemented to support maritime activities in the waters adjacent to Tierra del Fuego Island and the Antarctic sector, coastal ports, and the Exclusive Economic Zone

[1089] During this period, maritime traffic in the South Atlantic region (tourist cruises, fishing, and Antarctic activity) increased significantly

[1090] It is a comprehensive operation that addresses the diverse responsibilities assigned to the jurisdiction: search and rescue, the Annual Combined Patrol with Chile, support for Antarctic activities, maritime control and surveillance, and environmental protection

The Antarctic Policy of the Argentine Republic The Antarctic Policy is framed within the Antarctic Treaty, an international legal instrument signed in Washington on December

[1103] Ratified by the Argentine Republic and entered into force on June

[1104] Argentina believes that the full validity of the system of conventions, protocols, and other instruments of understanding established by the Antarctic Treaty is a necessary condition for the present and future development of that continent

[1105] It also views the Antarctic Treaty system as a guarantee for continuing to develop its active and ongoing scientific and conservation presence there

[1106] Within the terms of the Antarctic System, the Argentine State affirms its rights to sovereignty in the claimed sector, which does not inhibit cooperation with other countries in scientific research and the preservation of resources and the environment

[1107] In this context, and for the purposes of compliance with the international commitments acquired by the Nation in the Antarctic Treaty System, the “National Antarctic Policy” is issued

[1108] This policy makes explicit the country's strategic vision regarding the Antarctic sphere

[1109] This refers primarily to increasing Argentine influence in the decision-making process, promoting the protection of the Antarctic environment and its ecosystems, conserving fishery resources, deepening scientific and technological knowledge in the area, providing services to third parties—to facilitate transportation, supply, meteorology, and cartography—and preventing and resolving ecological contingencies and providing tourism-related services

[1113] In turn, the Navy contributes naval and air resources to the transport of general and scientific cargo, personnel transfers, search and rescue, and the deployment and redeployment of scientific and technical personnel, etc

[1117] In the same spirit, the Combined Antarctic Naval Patrol (PANC)—with human and material resources from the Argentine and Chilean Navies—conducts combined operations to safeguard human life at sea, control and combat pollution, and provide mutual support to address maritime emergencies in the waters surrounding the Antarctic continent

[1122] Part II Chapter X UNITED NATIONS STABILIZATION MISSION IN HAITI (MINUSTAH) The United Nations humanitarian intervention in Haiti began in February 1993, when a joint operation between the United Nations and the Organization of American States (OAS) was carried out on the island

[1123] In September 1993, the Security Council (UNSC) established the first United Nations peacekeeping operation in Haiti, known as the United Nations Mission in Haiti (UNMIH

[1124] A year later, the UNSC authorized the deployment of a multinational force of 20,000 troops to facilitate the return of legitimate authorities, maintain a secure and stable environment in the country, and promote the rule of law

[1125] The multinational force was followed by other United Nations missions between 1994 and 2001: the United Nations Support Mission in Haiti (UNSMIH), the United Nations Transition Mission in Haiti (UNTMIH), and the United Nations Civilian Police Mission in Haiti (MIPONUH

[1126] Argentine soldier performing duties in Haiti

[1127] In February 2004, the Security Council, in view of the political, social and economic fragility of Haiti, which seriously threatened peace, the rule of law and respect for human rights in that country, approved Resolution 1529 authorizing the deployment of the Interim Multinational Force (PMF

[1128] Barely a month later, taking into account the recommendations of the Secretary-General based on the conclusions of a multidisciplinary evaluation team that visited the Caribbean country, the Council unanimously approved another resolution, 1542, providing for the implementation of the United Nations Stabilization Mission in Haiti (MINUSTAH) for an initial period of six months, with the intention of extending it for further periods, as a stabilization and follow-up force to support the achievement of a peaceful and constitutional political process and maintain a safe and stable environment

[1129] In June 2004, the Argentine Congress authorized the participation of military personnel and material in MINUSTAH, the first United Nations peacekeeping mission. Argentine participation began in 1993, when the UNFICYP Task Force was formed – a regimental-sized element, comprising personnel from the Army, Navy and Air Force

[1141] This force carries out observation and incident reporting missions, with subsequent negotiations

[1145] UNITED NATIONS MISSION FOR THE REFERENDUM IN WESTERN SAHARA (MINURSO) Faced with the conflict between Morocco and the Sahrawi citizens (represented by the Popular Front for the Liberation of Saguia el-Hamra and Rio de Oro, Polisario Front) over the territory of Western Sahara, the United Nations and the Organization of African Unity (OAU) persuaded the parties involved of the need to initiate talks to reach an agreement

[1146] All of this led to Security Council Resolution 690 in 1991, which established MINURSO. It was deployed to supervise the ceasefire and organize and conduct a referendum in which the population of Western Sahara would have the opportunity to decide the future status of the territory

[1147] MINURSO's mandate initially consisted of supervising the ceasefire, verifying the reduction of Moroccan troops on the territory, supervising the restriction of Moroccan and Polisario troops at designated locations, taking measures with the parties to secure the release of all political prisoners or detainees in Western Sahara, supervising the exchange of prisoners of war (International Committee of the Red Cross), implementing the repatriation program (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees), identifying and registering persons eligible to vote, and organizing and ensuring the holding of a free and fair referendum to define the status of that region

[1148] Argentina's participation in the United Nations Mission became effective in 1991, when the Air Force deployed a military observer to the region, performing tasks such as desert patrols and transiting through minefields

[1149] Military observers from the Navy and Army are currently deployed

[1150] UNITED NATIONS TRUCE SUPERVISION AGENCY (UNTSO) The continuing conflict between the State of Israel and several neighbouring countries led the United Nations Security Council to call for a cessation of hostilities in that region as early as 1948 (Resolution

[1151] A truce was decided upon, to be supervised by a UN mediator assisted by a group of military observers

[1152] This is how UNTSO, the first peacekeeping operation created by the United Nations, was formed

[1153] Argentina has participated in this mission without interruption since 1967 and has observers in the region

[1154] Currently, all three forces (Army, Navy and Air Force) provide personnel

[1155] In addition to their mandate to monitor and report on violations of agreed treaties, observers perform additional tasks: verification of bombed areas and minefields, clearance of these areas, inspection of positions and cantonments, assistance in liaison between the parties to the conflict, and patrols and inspections of civilian settlements

[1156] OPERATIONS IN SUPPORT OF THE NATIONAL COMMUNITY OR FRIENDLY COUNTRIES The military instrument, within the framework of the fulfillment of its subsidiary missions, can use its capabilities in civil protection activities – both in support of the national community and that of friendly countries – in the face of natural disasters and emergencies that merit the comprehensive action of the State

[1157] This type of intervention contributes to the rational use of resources and to promoting efficient joint, joint-combined and interoperability standards between different national and foreign agencies or organizations

[1158] Air Force Hercules aircraft performing supply tasks

[1159] In this sense, the participation of the military instrument in civil protection operations allows, at the domestic level, the optimization of national capacities aimed at promoting the common good in its most diverse manifestations (social, economic, cultural, health, educational, sports, etc

[1160] Meanwhile, support for the community of friendly countries contributes to strengthening the processes of integration and collective development

[1161] Civil Defense's general functions include protection, understood as the set of actions carried out by State authorities to address the effects of nature and those produced by human intervention, in order to protect human life and public and private infrastructure, both in times of peace and armed conflict

[1162] Civil Defense, within the framework of National Defense, is an activity that encompasses nonaggressive measures and actions aimed at avoiding, nullifying, or reducing the effects that armed conflict, natural disasters, or any other disaster may have on the population, their property, or the environment

[1163] Its objective is to contribute to restoring the normal rhythm of life in the affected areas

[1164] In this sense, the participation of the Armed Forces in civil protection operations is framed within the materialization of subsidiary missions through three clearly differentiated modalities: - Humanitarian aid: this is the civil protection action carried out by the Armed Forces

[1165] in the country in cases of emergencies, catastrophes and critical social limitations, aimed at protecting human lives, infrastructure (public or private) and the environment

[1166] Humanitarian assistance: This is the form of civil protection carried out by the Armed Forces

[1167] to materialize federal support provided by the President of the Nation

[1168] This type of intervention is carried out in response to external requests—in the context of the United Nations—or as an act of international cooperation in the event of a catastrophe

[1169] In the latter case, its purpose is to contribute to strengthening the self-sufficiency capacities of communities affected by crises or endemic problems, focusing its activities primarily on food and health assistance and the establishment of shelters

[1170] Community support: includes tasks that the Armed Forces carry out without an emergency

[1171] with the purpose of promoting or facilitating the social and economic development of an area

[1172] The objective is to contribute to improving the quality of life and well-being of the population

[1173] Part II Chapter X

[1174] THE MILITARY INSTRUMENT IN THE FULFILLMENT OF SUBSIDIARY CIVIL PROTECTION MISSIONS Participation in operations to support the national or international community in the face of natural disasters constitutes a subsidiary mission of the military instrument, specifically regulated in the legal framework of National Defense

[1175] This framework includes the Federal Emergency System, specific regulations of the Ministry of Defense, and a series of international agreements

[1176] Such participation becomes effective when the resources already applied are considered insufficient

[1177] For these cases, agencies under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Defense participate in a rapid response structure, planned and directed by the Political Branch under the legal framework of the Federal Emergency System (SIFEM), which is activated when the Executive Branch declares a National Emergency

[1178] SIFEM is the national body that brings together the relevant public agencies and coordinates their actions with the provinces, the Government of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, and the municipalities, with the goal of preventing and managing emergencies and disasters of natural or man-made origin

[1179] The Ministry of Defense jurisdiction participates through its head—a member of the Emergency Cabinet (GADE), the body that leads and coordinates the system during an emergency—and with the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces (EMCO), the General Staffs of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, the Institute of Scientific and Technical Research for Defense (CITEDEF), the National Geographic Institute, the National Meteorological Service, the Naval Hydrography Service, and the Secretariat of Strategy and Military Affairs as base organizations

[1180] Likewise, the Minister of Defense and the EMCO participate in the National Commission for Monitoring Emergencies and Disasters (CONAMED) along with other national agencies (Federal Police, Gendarmerie, Naval Prefecture, Airport Security Police, National Directorate of Health Emergencies, National Directorate of Social Emergencies, Secretariat of the Environment, Naval Hydrography Service, and National Meteorological Service

[1181] CONAMED's activities are part of the National Directorate of Civil Protection, which reports to the Undersecretariat of Security of the Ministry of the Interior

[1182] Under these parameters, the EMCO assumes the coordination and direction—through the Operational Command—of civil protection operations and activities in those cases in which the Ministry of Defense or national authorities determine the use of the Armed Forces to meet the requirements of the SIFEM—both domestically and abroad

[1183] In this way, at the national level, the military instrument participates in humanitarian aid activities in emergency situations or natural disasters and in tasks of support to the local community, to promote the social and economic development of an area, under the modality of complementary effort of humanitarian aid

[1184] In the latter case, these include educational activities, school sponsorship, and cultural and sports activities

[1185] At the international level, and in line with the drive for regional integration that guides Argentina's foreign policy, the military instrument carries out civil protection activities in support of friendly countries—with or without the activation of international cooperation agreements—under the category of humanitarian assistance

[1186] Thus, with regard to civil protection activities, the military instrument is responsible for carrying out activities related to: - Organization of emergency operations centers: deployment of facilities, communications, computer resources, security, and personnel specialized in planning and management

[1273] Part III MILITARY EXERCISES Chapter XI In a comprehensive conception of national defense, military exercises transcend the importance of their technical-military dimension to become, as occurs with combined exercises, significant activities of both the defense policy and the foreign policy of the nation

[1274] SPECIFIC, JOINT AND COMBINED MILITARY EXERCISES

[1275] Within the framework of normal training, military exercises are conceptualized as activities developed through the application of techniques, skills, and abilities to increase, verify, and consolidate the level of acquired capabilities

[1276] The exercises carried out by the Armed Forces in recent years are classified—depending on whether or not they involve the use of operational capabilities—as desk exercises or simulation exercises and field exercises

[1277] In turn, ground forces can be defined as specific, joint or combined, depending on the composition and origin of the forces involved

[1278] Specific: those in which the means of a single armed force participate

[1279] These are planned and executed by this force within the framework duly defined by Joint Military Planning

[1280] Joint forces: these are those in which elements of two or more forces from the same country participate

[1281] These are planned and executed under the direction of EMCO

[1282] Combined: are those in which the Armed Forces participate

[1283] of two or more countries under a centralized command and with a common purpose

[1284] They are planned and coordinated by representatives of the intervening forces and executed under the direction of a centralized combined command

[1285] The determination of these exercises from the Argentine side is carried out within the framework of what was duly defined by the Joint Military Planning

[1286] These exercises can be joint or specific

[1287] Joint-combined exercises: those in which personnel and material from two or more Armed Forces participate

[1288] from a country with two or more armed forces

[1289] from other countries

[1290] Part II Chapter XI - Specific-Combined Exercises: are those in which personnel and material from a specific armed force participate with its counterpart from another country or countries

[1291] Specific and joint exercises of the Armed Forces promote the increase in the operational skills of the military instrument

[1292] In this way, they consolidate joint military action, allow for the diagnosis of the operational capacity of available military units, and deepen knowledge and control of the geographic environment and operational areas

[1293] Combined exercises contribute to the political dimension of National Defense, as they contribute to increasing and consolidating mutual trust among states and are essential for building a subregional defense system, while also contributing to strengthening the South American region as a "zone of peace

[1294] Furthermore, from a technical military perspective, combined exercises increase and test the military's interoperability with third nations, a practice regularly implemented in United Nations peacekeeping missions

[1295] PRIORITIZATION CRITERIA FOR MILITARY EXERCISES Regarding joint military exercises, the prioritization criteria and general orientation are related to: - The achievement, maintenance and consolidation of optimal levels of training and operational aptitude of the military forces, in order to enable the effective fulfillment of the main mission and the subsidiary missions of the military instrument

[1296] The optimization of joint military action standards, joint employment doctrine, and operational integration of armed forces capabilities

[1297] as well as the activities of planning, conducting and executing operations

[1298] The prevalence of those exercises in which the necessary resources-already deployed on the ground-allow for their parallel use to support the community where the exercises are conducted

[1299] The deepening and consolidation of the joint activity of the Armed Forces

[1300] with national civil agencies and organizations that have direct responsibility for supporting the community in disaster situations, with the aim of achieving greater levels of interagency coordination

[1301] In relation to combined military exercises (bilateral or multilateral, specific or joint), the criteria that have guided their prioritization in recent years have been: - The promotion and strengthening of mutual trust and the deepening of the levels of military interoperability with other Armed Forces

[1302] at the regional and subregional levels

[1303] The development and consolidation of skills related to the primary mission of the military instrument and participation in multilateral exercises within the framework of the collective security system (peacekeeping operations in their various forms), and further development in operations to support the national community or friendly countries in the event of catastrophes or natural disasters

[1304] The concrete increase and verification of our own capability levels and the degree of military interoperability with regional and subregional nations

[1305] Along the same lines, the incorporation of recently created operational codes and procedures and the promotion of the development, modernization, and consolidation of combined operational doctrine with these countries

[1306] The optimization of the capabilities required for combined activities involving the planning, management, and execution of field operations

[1307] Obtaining specific parameters for the design and determination of the capabilities of the military instrument

[1308] Parameters that refer to the achievement and consolidation of minimum interoperability standards for efficient military interaction of an expanded and multilateral nature

[1309] The consolidation of codes and procedures aimed at promoting greater levels of understanding and coordination in the event of crises or contingencies

[1310] JOINT MILITARY EXERCISES This type of exercise covers different aspects of military training, from those related to the main mission of the military instrument to those related to subsidiary missions

[1311] The ultimate objective is the consolidation of joint military action and the effective integration of the Armed Forces, with a view to fulfilling the primary mission

[1312] Below are some of the joint exercises carried out in recent years: - The “H-20” Exercise stands out, carried out in November 2008, in which nearly three thousand personnel from the Army, Navy and Air Force participated
