[1339] Source: Ministry of Defense Part III TRANSFORMATION OF THE DEFENSE SYSTEM The precedent represented by the promulgation of the National Defense Law in 1988 allowed successive national administrations to contribute to building, with different contributions, the legal framework to resolve some of the fundamental issues of the Defense System: a) the consolidation of the subordination of the Armed Forces to the constitutional order, and b) the conceptual differentiation of National Defense and Internal Security, through an explicit definition of the missions and functions of the Armed Forces and the security forces

[1340] Although Argentina had established a solid regulatory framework by the beginning of the 21st century, it still needed to activate it and embark on a process of systemic redesign of the sector—particularly its military instrument—that would allow for the adaptation of organizational structures that had been designed in the strategic context of the Cold War (or even earlier) to a new international reality and a new internal situation in terms of resources

[1341] Two decades after the only conventional conflict involving the Argentine Republic in the 20th century, its defense system still suffered from a series of organizational and functional inconsistencies that, along with budget cuts, had contributed to a deterioration in its capabilities

[1342] These institutional weaknesses were present in various dimensions: political, regulatory, planning, logistical, operational, doctrinal, and training

[1343] The lack of integration and joint military action, with the negative impact it had on operational performance during the Falklands War, remained an unresolved issue

[1344] Part III The transformation process Chapter XII

[1345] DIAGNOSIS OF THE DEFENSE SYSTEM At the beginning of the 21st century, the national defense system presented a set of structural dysfunctions that had contributed to plunging the military instrument into a deep existential crisis

[1346] Among them, the following stand out: Strategic disorientation

[1347] Lack of guidelines originating from senior political leadership that would establish precise guidelines for comprehensively guiding defense and military policy

[1348] Absence of a strategic planning dynamic that would combine the assessment of the international environment with a coherent national integration strategy and a consistent model of military instrument for the medium and long term

[1349] Use of a planning methodology based on anachronistic hypotheses of conflicts with neighboring countries, now trade and political partners. The regulatory and institutional framework is incomplete

[1350] Lack of regulation of the National Defense Law, a central legal instrument for coordinating the missions and functions of the organizations comprising the Defense System

[1351] Formal nonexistence or non-functioning of key bodies and agencies provided for in the regulatory framework, such as the National Defense Council itself or the Joint Operational Command

[1352] Absence of joint military organization and action

[1353] The continuation of a compartmentalized model of organization and operation, where each armed force planned, equipped, trained, and operated separately and without coordination

[1354] Structural weakness of the Joint Chiefs of Staff

[1355] Disregard for the recommendations of the Rattenbach Commission report following the Falklands War. Obsolescence and material degradation

[1356] Product of continued net disinvestment in equipment and infrastructure and inadequate maintenance of existing capital stock

[1357] Part III Chapter XII Structural inefficiency

[1358] Suboptimal management of the sector's resources, with fragmented efforts among the three Armed Forces for the supply, maintenance, transportation, and storage of goods and services commonly consumed by the forces. Disarticulation of science and technology

[1359] Lack of links between the areas of science and technology within the Armed Forces, including the Ministry of Defense itself and the National Science and Technology System

[1360] Dissociation between technological development projects and the medium- and long-term material needs of the military instrument

[1361] Dismantling of the defense industry

[1362] The privatization process of the 1990s involved the dissolution of the industrial production network that included heavy metallurgy, portable weapons factories, combat vehicles, shipyards, and aircraft production

[1363] Subsistence of outdated training models

[1364] Inconsistency between training methodologies and content and the standards required for the instruction of military professionals within the framework of a modern democratic system

[1365] Triplication of efforts devoted to the same type of specialized training. Disorganization of the military intelligence subsystem

[1366] The military intelligence agencies produced, in an overlapping manner, the same level of intelligence (military strategic intelligence) as the National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence

[1367] Failure to update the specific intelligence regulations of the Armed Forces to comply with the principles of the National Defense (exclusion from the internal sphere) and National Intelligence laws

[1368] Continuation of practices and regulations that violate human rights

[1369] Persistence of institutional practices and regulations contrary to national legislation or international instruments for the protection of human rights, such as the obligation to provide information on aspects of private life or the requirement of authorization from a superior to enter into marriage, among others

[1370] Gender inequality

[1371] Persistence of discriminatory practices against women and absence of policies to equalize career opportunities

[1372] Anachronistic Military Justice System

[1373] Citizens of the military profession were deprived of a series of basic civil rights, with regulations contrary to the National Constitution and international instruments for the protection of human rights persisting since colonial times

[1374] Civil functions under the responsibility of the Armed Forces

[1375] Denaturalization of the missions and functions of the military instrument, keeping them under the jurisdiction of the Armed Forces

[1376] areas such as civil aviation, airport security, meteorological service, weapons registration, among others

[1377] Lack of coordination with the internal security system

[1378] Lack of institutionalized procedures for coordination with the internal security system regarding legally provided shared utility functions, such as airspace surveillance

[1379] Following the return to democracy in 1983, the country experienced periods of political and institutional fragility, as demonstrated by four military uprisings in the late 1980s, in parallel with marked economic instability

[1380] The defense sector was not immune to the country's general difficulties

[1381] However, these contextual conditions alone do not explain the described picture of dysfunctions

[1382] During the two decades following the restoration of democracy, the institutional imbalances in the sector were accentuated by the absence of a comprehensive redesign of the system, led by the Executive Branch, that would modernize its doctrinal, organizational, and functional aspects

[1383] For this reason, it is necessary to introduce two specific factors with strong explanatory power: a delegative attitude toward the political management of defense, and the progressive distortion of the budget with the minimum level of resources necessary to sustain the inherited structure of the system

[1384] THE DELEGATIVE ATTITUDE OF THE POLITICAL MANAGEMENT OF DEFENSE In general terms and for years, an attitude of political management of defense predominated in which the civil authorities formally exercised command but delegated its effective leadership to military leaders

[1385] This meant entrusting their military subordinates with responsibility for the design, planning, and oversight of defense policies, as well as for the organization and operation of the military apparatus

[1386] This management attitude consolidated a delegative mechanism that implied that the political authorities voluntarily ceded autonomy to the military authorities, avoiding or postponing political definitions on central issues for the proper functioning of the Defense System, such as the specification of missions and functions of the military instrument, the establishment of resizing criteria or the development of planning strategies that went beyond schemes based on outdated conflict hypotheses

[1387] Consequently, the military leadership assumed, in an inorganic manner, powers and functions not exercised by the national strategic level, with the resulting lack of overall coherence and disarticulation for the system

[1388] In this way, the institutional evolution of each of the forces was inevitably tied to definitions of circumstantial, partial, and specific logic

[1389] Progressive Distortion of the Defense Budget In the years following the restoration of democracy, the budget allocation was drastically reduced both in terms of its share in the national budget and in the gross domestic product (GDP), without such adjustment process responding, as we have seen, to an orderly planning

[1390] This led to a systematic and progressive distortion of the defense budget

[1391] Several factors explain this drop in the budget

[1392] First, the emerging political and social consensus following the restoration of democracy implied a reorientation of fiscal efforts toward other development priorities

[1393] Secondly, the process of détente, cooperation, and integration among the region's states—especially in the Southern Cone—has reduced the likelihood of interstate armed conflicts, consequently reducing the perception of risk and the social legitimacy of defense spending

[1394] This downsizing would not have been so detrimental to the Defense System, however, if the political authorities had not delegated the options for cuts and restructuring to the military authorities themselves

[1395] In the absence of political guidelines that would allow for the development of a new systemic design of force, these forces proceeded to resize themselves without any order or strategic criteria

[1396] Consequently, without political guidelines that would provide a rational basis for adjustment, military leaders eliminated, cut back, or deprogrammed units and weapons systems, reduced operational training to minimal levels, relaxed maintenance standards, and normalized emergency logistical measures, such as the consumption of spare parts and ammunition reserves

[1397] Sinking aimlessly into a constant crisis, they attempted, to the best of their ability, to sustain inherited but increasingly irrational structures, awaiting a reversal of the resource-contraction trend, which never came

[1398] Part III Chapter XII Within the framework of this chaotic contractive dynamic, the scarcity of resources was aggravated by the inefficient use of those available: the chronic budgetary problem lay not only in its quantitative dimension but also in its qualitative application, that is, in the quality of its administration

[1399] In a scenario of severe constraint in which "fixed costs" in personnel matters represented the bulk of the budget, suboptimal management of the resources available for variable costs was unacceptable

[1400] This reality became a constant in which spending was applied unnecessarily and redundantly due to the lack of integration between the Armed Forces. This implied, for example, the proliferation of identical technological developments, the simultaneous maintenance of triple maintenance structures for common weapons systems, training and instruction activities that could be integrated, or the acquisition of common inputs in multiple automated procedures, thus disregarding the advantages of economies of scale and the achievement of synergies

[1401] The quotation marks refer to the fact that in traditional economic theory the cost of labor (salary) represents a variable cost

[1402] However, in public administration, workforce adjustment tends to be much more inelastic than in the private sector, hence its treatment as a fixed cost

[1406] Axes of Transformation To reverse the general dysfunctions of the Defense System, a process of structural transformation was proposed with two general objectives: The consolidation of an effective civilian defense government. The modernization of the Defense System with the aim of providing it with strategic coherence, operational effectiveness, and systemic efficiency

[1407] The modernization of the Defense System with the aim of providing it with strategic coherence, operational effectiveness, and systemic efficiency

[1408] The first objective, the effective exercise of civilian governance of the Defense System, was in fact considered a necessary condition for achieving the second, given that, by virtue of its powers, the highest leadership is the only body that can make decisions binding on all components of the system

[1409] The modernization of the system required a comprehensive process involving the Ministry of Defense itself, its decentralized bodies, and the Armed Forces: At the ministerial level, the process was aimed at strengthening its legally assigned powers and providing it with new management capabilities, based on a series of regulations of varying hierarchy (parliamentary, presidential, and ministerial), and by strengthening its institutional architecture through new specialized political and technical structures

[1410] The modernization of the Armed Forces involved: a) modifying the parameters regarding missions, functions, conception, and criteria for the effective use of military instruments; b) redesigning the architecture and the normative, organizational, and functional framework; c) changing the strategic planning methodology; d) reformulating the subsystems of human resources, infrastructure, logistics, materiel, training, organization, information, and doctrine

[1411] Based on these objectives, the transformation process adopted a defense organization paradigm structured around the following axes: Definition of a strategic posture

[1412] Adoption of a defensive conception, positioning, and strategic attitude based on the principle of self-defense as the essential and organizing criterion that structures the national defense model, with an autonomous and cooperative approach

[1413] This concept is consistent with the eventual establishment of a regional defense system and cooperates with the multilateral system in its efforts for international peace and security

[1414] Consolidation of the institutional architecture of the National Defense System

[1415] Establishment of an organizational architecture that implies, in terms of its levels of competence and responsibilities, that the Ministry of Defense (national strategic level) designs, determines, and guides defense and military policies; the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces (advisory body to the Ministry of Defense at the military strategic level) plans, executes, and supervises; while the Armed Forces

[1416] tactical operational level) prepare, train and sustain military means of defense

[1417] Thus, the defense is structured organically and functionally according to the missions, obligations and procedural characteristics of each instance

[1418] Strengthening the organic structure for the effective exercise of civil government

[1419] Consolidation of the Ministry of Defense's political, technical, and administrative capabilities, encompassing and involving all management dimensions

[1420] Principle of joint action

[1421] Formation of an integrated military instrument that is organized and operates based on the guiding principle of “joint military action.”

[1422] This principle extends to doctrine, planning, formation, training, logistics, and operations

[1423] From an organizational perspective, this means strengthening the Joint Chiefs of Staff (EMCO), the highest military advisory body at the national strategic level and responsible for conducting all peacetime military operations and joint military planning

[1424] He is also responsible for designing the profile of the military instrument's operational capabilities, from which the sizing and deployment of human resources and weapons systems are derived

[1425] Meanwhile, with the creation of the Operational Command within the EMCO, all military operations in peacetime are centralized

[1426] Budget design derived from strategic planning

[1427] Institutionalization of a defense planning framework that articulates strategic objectives with multiyear programs and annual budgeting, ensuring that allocations are consistent with the material priorities of the military instrument

[1428] Integrated production of strategic knowledge

[1429] Integration of the capacity to produce strategic knowledge for understanding international dynamics and to jointly assist in the formulation of defense policy and the planning process

[1430] Optimization of the resource management system

[1431] Development of an integrated logistics system for the defense system, capable of effectively and efficiently meeting the material requirements determined by strategic planning, encompassing both the procurement of equipment and infrastructure (genetic logistics) and their maintenance (sustainment logistics

[1432] Integration of research and technological development

[1433] Institutionalization of a defense science, technology, and production system integrated into the national scientific and technological system, which involves: a) internal coordination of all defense research and development organizations; b) matching the technological offering with the development and resource requirements arising from strategic defense planning; and c) coordinating technological development with the defense production sector. Recovery of the defense industry

[1434] Recovering the capabilities of the defense production network with the simultaneous objective of providing the military with increasing technological and industrial autonomy and contributing to the country's development through the generation of value chains (clusters

[1435] Modernization of the training system

[1436] Redesign of the defense education system to integrate military training institutes and civilian training institutes into the national education system

[1437] Strengthening the civic education of military personnel as specialized public officials through the inclusion of cross-curricular content on Constitutional and Administrative Law, Human Rights, and International Humanitarian Law

[1438] Promoting the establishment of joint training courses in various specialties and joint use of existing infrastructure. Adapting defense intelligence to current regulations

[1439] Consolidation of a Defense Intelligence subsystem: a) harmoniously integrated into the National Intelligence System; b) articulated into its various components; c) operating in accordance with the National Intelligence Law, democratic principles and values, and criteria of functionality and efficiency; d) led by the Ministry of Defense through the guidance, coordination, and supervision of intelligence production activities carried out by the intelligence agencies of the Armed Forces

[1440] Part III Chapter XII Implementation of a cross-cutting human rights policy

[1441] Incorporation and promotion of the human rights perspective as a necessary condition for strengthening an institutional culture based on democratic principles, values, and practices

[1442] Creation of mechanisms for monitoring rights and guarantees; access to public information; reception and processing of cases and complaints of abuse of authority; elimination of discriminatory or privacy-invasive regulations; repeal of the old military justice system; and adaptation of regulations to the requirements of the National Constitution and international instruments for the protection of fundamental human rights

[1443] Gender perspectives: equalizing professional opportunities for women

[1444] Consolidation of a gender perspective that involves reconciling the responsibilities of professional activity and the family obligations of military and civilian personnel: promoting equal access and advancement

[1445] Eradication of gender-based violence and all forms of discrimination in the military

[1446] Demilitarization of civil functions

[1447] Transfer to competent civilian authorities of various functions and activities originally carried out by the Armed Forces

[1448] which were outside their main or subsidiary mission: Commercial air traffic management, airport security, meteorological service, hydrographic service, pension management, registration of personal weapons

[1449] launch of the Aspide missile from the Meko 140 Corvette

[1450] Part III Chapter XII Development of transparency mechanisms

[1451] Strengthening institutional transparency through mechanisms for access to information, greater disaggregation of budget disclosures, oversight of procurement, and promotion of reporting of corruption

[1452] Incorporating environmental responsibility into defense activities and developing initiatives for the preservation of environmental heritage in natural areas used by the Armed Forces. Personnel rights and well-being

[1453] Recognition of civil rights for defense personnel and promotion of access to social rights

[1454] Systematization and expansion of housing access programs and optimization of services provided by the defense health system

[1455] training of soldiers of the Argentine army

[1456] Part III Chapter XIII STRENGTHENING THE MINISTRY OF DEFENSE Strengthening the political leadership body constitutes the logical starting point for the process of transforming the defense system because it is within it that the guidelines for the design, planning, organization and operation of the military instrument are formulated, and its subsequent implementation is also supervised. To achieve this strengthening, three types of interventions were implemented: 1) making the mandates of the existing legal framework for defense operational; 2) expanding the allocation of specific powers to the Ministry of Defense; and 3) incorporating specialized organizational units into the structure of the Ministry to enhance its management capacity

[1457] In relation to the first intervention, the National Defense Law was regulated, the National Defense Council (CODENA) was put into operation, and the operational framework for the organization of the Armed Forces and strategic planning was defined

[1458] These regulations also assigned the Ministry of Defense new specific powers in matters of political leadership, ranging from strategic planning to senior leadership and administration of the military instrument

[1459] In connection with the third intervention, the Ministry's structure was modified, creating new organizational units at different levels to address responsibilities in various areas: strategic planning, resource management, logistics, science and technology, industrial production, training, strategic intelligence, human rights, gender equity, staff well-being, institutional transparency, and international cooperation

[1460] IMPLEMENTATION OF THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK 1.1 REGULATION OF THE NATIONAL DEFENSE LAW The regulation of this law constituted an act of political will to reverse the traditional delegative attitude in the management of defense and to make effective the orderly functioning of the institutional architecture by specifying in detail the missions and functions of each component of the system: the Ministry of Defense, the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Armed Forces

[1461] Among its central determinations are: a) The strengthening of the Ministry of Defense as the body for the conduction, planning, implementation and supervision of defense policy and its derived military policy, as well as the administration and superior leadership of the Armed Forces

[1462] b) Strengthening the role of the Joint Chiefs of Staff as the highest authority for military advice to the national political leadership, responsible for developing joint military strategic planning and submitting it to the Ministry, for developing joint doctrine and training, and as the sole body responsible for all military operations through its Operational Command

[1463] The precise definition of the missions and functions of the military instrument, limiting the concept of "external aggression" exclusively to those of a military and state nature; and limiting the missions and functions of the Armed Forces to preparing, training, and maintaining the resources at their disposal to ensure their effective use within the framework of military strategic planning

[1468] “The existence of the Ministry of Defense is an important basic indicator of the quality of civil-military relations in a country” The first function of a Ministry of Defense is to “structure the relations between democratically elected civilian leaders and the General Staffs of the Armed Forces.”

[1469] The second is to “define and distribute responsibilities between civilians and military officers.”

[1470] The third is to “maximize the effectiveness of the employment of the Armed Forces.”

[1471] That is, the ability to implement policies with the military instrument

[1472] Fourth, you must “maximize resource efficiency”: achieve your assigned missions at the lowest cost

[1473] Finally, the Ministry must establish a balance between the components of the military instrument and promote "comprehensiveness

[1474] To carry out these functions, the Ministry of Defense must have jurisdiction, both in regulations and in practice, over at least the following areas: a) Definition of the missions and functions of the military instrument; b) Definition of the budget, distribution of resources, and oversight of its execution; c) Definition of personnel matters, in terms of structure, career, promotions, assignments, and training; d) Intervention in the procurement process

[1480] CALL FOR THE NATIONAL DEFENSE COUNCIL (CODENA) The National Defense Council is a key body within the Defense System, as its advice and assistance constitute the cornerstone for establishing the major political guidelines for the sector

[1481] The CODENA - formally created by the National Defense Law - was convened in 2006 and, in accordance with the provisions of the law, the National Executive Branch required it to carry out a "Comprehensive diagnosis of the national strategic situation

[1482] Its implementation represented a substantial contribution to the institutionalization of defense policy, as it produced with the participation of all ministries, the Defense Committees of both chambers of the National Congress, the State's highest intelligence agency, the General Staffs of each Armed Force, and the Joint Chiefs of Staff—the first institutional assessment of the Argentine Republic formulated from a specific approach to the defense sector since the return of democracy

[1483] This enabled the start of the new National Defense Planning Cycle, one of the structural elements of the process of transforming the Defense System

[1484] DIRECTIVE ON THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATION OF THE ARMED FORCES The Directive on the organization and operation of the Armed Forces, a document proposed by the Ministry of Defense and approved by the Executive Branch in 2006, is the first political document with a technical-military content that defines the guiding parameters of the missions, the conception and criteria for the employment, organization, redesign of capabilities and equipment of the Armed Forces

[1485] This directive advances the definition of the general guidelines for defense policy—which define how the State seeks to safeguard and protect the nation's values and assets through a specific conception and design profile of operational capabilities—and explicitly structuring criteria for the organization, operation, and equipment of the military instrument

[1486] The "Comprehensive Diagnosis of the National Strategic Situation" contains a description and analysis of the factors that represent or could represent "vulnerabilities" for the Argentine Republic, specifically for its defense

[1487] To this end, it systematically analyzed the concept of "national vulnerability," understood as the sum of those factors inherent to weakness and deficiency that restrict the country's freedom of action, capabilities, and relative position, potentially causing various harm and preventing it from benefiting from opportunities or acting as risks when a strategic will emerges in opposition, willing or able to use these weaknesses to its advantage

[1491] Part III Chapter XIII From the highest strategic leadership level, this document defines core issues for the military instrument: a) The main and subsidiary missions of the military instrument and their respective areas of action; b) The conception of the military instrument and the conditions for its effective use; c) The roles and functions of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Armed Forces; d) The redesign of the military instrument based on the Argentine Republic's defensive positioning; e) Criteria for guiding the allocation of priorities to the military instrument's capabilities and the equipment alternatives for achieving them

[1492] In methodological terms, these definitions implied the replacement of the conflict-hypothesis-based planning methodology with military capabilities-based planning

[1493] DEFENSE PLANNING CYCLE The National Defense Planning Cycle, established in 2007 by Executive Decree, involves putting in place an institutional mechanism that links the national and military strategic levels, allowing for civil leadership over all instances of defense planning

[1494] This cycle begins with the approval by the Executive Branch of a “National Defense Policy Directive” (DPDN

[1495] From that point on, and under the supervision of the Ministry, the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces proposes military strategic planning, having convened the planning bodies of the three Armed Forces for this purpose

[1496] This regulation grants the Ministry of Defense the authority to propose the basic document for the "DPDN" to the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, oversee the development of the cycle, order corrections, and approve the subsequent documents that comprise it

[1497] Along with the implementation of the legal framework for defense, the Ministry of Defense was strengthened as the body for “direction, organization and coordination of defense activities”9, through the assignment of specific powers for the superior management of the military instrument, national strategic planning, military strategic planning and the administration of the military instrument

[1521] CONSOLIDATION OF THE ORGANIC STRUCTURE The organic structure of the Ministry of Defense was modified five times during the first decade of the 21st century

[1522] The starting point is given by the organizational structure approved in February 2000. It comprises, at the political level, two Secretariats (Military Affairs and Planning) and an Undersecretariat (Coordination), while the assistance body at the political level comprised a total of eight general directorates, six of which were for technical advice and two for administrative support

[1523] In 2002, a National Directorate (Intelligence) was added, and while a General Directorate for administrative support was added, two technical advisory offices were reduced

[1524] In 2003, the political bodies of the Ministry were revised, creating two Undersecretariats (Institutional Strengthening and Technical-Military Affairs) and maintaining the number of General Directorates constant

[1525] In 2006, a new National Directorate (Human Rights) was created

[1526] In 2007, a quantitative and qualitative transformation of the Ministry of Defense began

[1527] At the political level, a new Secretariat (International Affairs) is established, two existing Undersecretariats are modified, and two new ones are created (Training and Research and Development

[1528] At the technical level, the general support directorates remain in place, but five new technical advisory units have been created, covering management areas such as peacekeeping operations, training, research and development, and logistics and industrial planning

[1529] The last adjustment corresponds to 2008 and added a General Directorate of Advisory Services (Strategic Planning) and the General Directorate of the Defense Logistics Service, the complexity of which will be addressed in a specific chapter

[1530] The creation of these units with specific powers allowed for a functionally comprehensive development of sector planning, the systemic execution of plans and programs, and the exercise of civil leadership through political, technical, and administrative levels that assumed powers previously delegated without coordination within the Armed Forces

[1531] The linking of requirements for the transformation of the Defense System with the creation of new organizational units in the Ministry of Defense can be illustrated by the following cases: 1) The creation of the Secretariat of International Defense Affairs allows for the comprehensive management of military representations abroad, based on the priorities of the Nation's foreign policy and criteria that respond to the requirements of the Defense System

[1575] BUDGET TRANSPARENCY One of the structural bases of the public budget system is the application of the Program Budget technique, which together with the classifiers allows the Budget and its main results to be objectively presented

[1576] In this context, the development of the programmatic structure of the Defense jurisdiction involves carrying out a process of collecting, processing and analyzing the information required to know what results the institution seeks, what it does to achieve them, who does it, how it does it, and with how many resources

[1577] As a result of a substantial review of these parameters over the last decade, a significant evolution in the jurisdiction's programmatic openness can be seen

[1578] The above evolution demonstrates the progress made in the disaggregation of the programmatic opening of the defense budget, which is directly proportional to greater rigor in the application of technical reporting criteria and represents a key contribution to transparency in the management of resources

[1579] In this regard, based on the 2007 defense budget, any citizen-taxpayer can learn the magnitude and composition of resources allocated to functions such as training, maintenance, research and development, tactical intelligence, modernization programs, officer and non-commissioned officer training, among others

[1580] The defense budget broken down into these categories can be consulted on the National Budget Office website

[1598] EXERCISE OF LEADERSHIP The issuance of ministerial resolutions (a top-level regulation approved by the relevant minister) is an indicator that allows measuring the levels and scope of the leadership of the Defense System

[1599] In this sense, resolutions are classified into two types: Structural resolutions: those that establish planning, execution and control systems for substantive defense functions

[1600] They establish criteria, establish guidelines and regulate processes, thus integrating the Defense Doctrine

[1601] Administrative resolutions: those that formalize a routine and insubstantial act of ministerial management (travel authorizations, verdicts on the applicability of assistance regimes, internal budget adjustments, lower-level appointments, among others

[1602] Between 2000 and 2009, the Ministry of Defense issued 14,397 ministerial resolutions

[1603] Of this total, more than 98% corresponded to administrative resolutions

[1623] At the political-strategic level, the transformation adopted a defensive international conception and positioning

[1624] In this way, the new position is emerging by replacing old conflict hypotheses with an ascending chain of convergence hypotheses, measures of trust, cooperation, and integration with neighbors

[1625] And, as described in previous chapters, with strategic planning by capabilities

[1626] In order to implement this concept, a specific political body was established within the organic structure of the Ministry of Defense: the Secretariat of International Defense Affairs, responsible for planning and executing in a coherent and coordinated manner the political and institutional link with the Ministries of Defense and the Armed Forces of other countries, and with multilateral defense organizations

[1627] PEN Decree

[1628] FUNDAMENTALS OF THE INTERNATIONAL POSITIONING OF DEFENSE National defense is founded and guided by the unequivocal respect and promotion of democracy, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States, the self-determination of peoples, respect for human rights, the vocation for peace and justice, and adherence to and observance of international law and the multilateral system as irreplaceable instruments for regulating relations and resolving conflicts between nations

[1629] Argentina also firmly believes that cooperation among States in defense matters is the means to build and consolidate international trust, peace, and security

[1630] Within the framework of these principles, the international dimension of Argentine defense adopts as its general objectives the promotion and consolidation of South America as a "zone of peace" and the progressive construction of a subregional defense system, as well as contributing to efforts aimed at extending and maintaining international peace and security

[1631] These objectives of National defense in a legal framework articulated by successive democratic governments, configure a State policy that is summarized in the following guidelines: - Model of international insertion that starts from a conception, positioning and strategic attitude of defensive nature and character, as has been described in Chapter III

[1632] A vocation for the construction of a subregional defense framework and a permanent commitment to and collaboration with multilateral efforts for international peace and security, confirmed by multiple actions ranging from participation in peacekeeping operations mandated by the United Nations to non-proliferation regimes and the control of the transfer of sensitive war material

[1633] Political-institutional architecture in which the Ministry of Defense establishes political-strategic relationships with other defense ministries, as well as the technical-professional interactions of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Armed Forces with their international counterparts

[1634] Consequently, the international military ties and actions of our Armed Forces are fully aligned with the directives duly established by the nation's defense and foreign policies

[1635] The implementation of these guidelines is reflected in the following policies: - The qualitative progress of cooperation with the nations of Latin America in general and South America in particular

[1636] All of this is intended to strengthen the process of regional cooperation and integration and consolidate this region as a zone of peace

[1637] Thus, defense policy promotes: a) strategic dialogue at the political and military levels, and the effective and regular operation of permanent institutional mechanisms with the Ministries of Defense and the Armed Forces of the countries in the region; b) the updating of existing bilateral agreements and the signing of new ones with countries with which they were not previously registered; c) experiences in cooperation and integration, such as the Argentine-Chilean Combined Binational Peacekeeping Force "Cruz del Sur" and the Peruvian-Argentine Combined Engineering Company "General San Martín"; d) the implementation of the "defense cooperation program" to replace traditional military or naval cooperation missions; e) close institutional relations and a variety of technical and professional exercises and exchanges between the Argentine Armed Forces and their regional counterparts; f) scientific, technological, and production complementarity projects for defense; and g) proactive support for the creation and consolidation of the South American Defense Council (CDS

[1638] In line with Latin American foreign policy, agreements were signed and defense exchanges and cooperation actions were carried out with Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela

[1639] Commitment to regional multilateral initiatives, which contribute to strengthening international peace and security mechanisms

[1640] In this context, it is worth mentioning the Latin American Association of Peacekeeping Operations Training Centers (ALCOPAZ), the active participation in the "2x9" mechanism for Haiti, the obtaining of observer status in the Conference of Central American Armed Forces (CFAC), and active membership in the Conference of Defense Ministers of the Americas

[1641] The use of defense human and material resources for humanitarian assistance in the event of catastrophes and natural disasters in countries in the region

[1642] The deepening of defense cooperation and exchange relations with extra-regional nations

[1643] First Conference of Ombudsman Institutions of the Armed Forces, held in Berlin, Germany

[1644] The reaffirmation of a continuous contribution for more than fifty years in peacekeeping operations under the United Nations flag

[1645] Our Armed Forces have participated in more than thirty missions throughout their history, deploying more than forty thousand troops

[1646] Regional Priorities The priorities of international defense policy relating to areas of strategic interest can be illustrated by a scheme of concentric circles ranging from the subregional to the global

[1647] South America represents the priority space for institutional presence and cooperation and complementarity in defense matters, followed successively by Latin America, the American continent, and then the regions and actors relevant to our interests in the rest of the world

[1651] The objective is to develop cooperation schemes that result in mutual benefit for the parties, involve the transfer of technology and knowledge, and strengthen interoperability capabilities, all of which contribute to ensuring the sustainability and development of cooperative defense relations

[1654] The Question of Sovereignty over the Malvinas Islands in the Context of Defense Policy As indicated in Chapter III, the Argentine Constitution claims legitimate and imprescriptible sovereignty over the Malvinas, South Georgia and South Sandwich Islands and the corresponding maritime and insular spaces, as they are an integral part of the national territory

[1655] The recovery of these territories and the full exercise of sovereignty, respecting the way of life of their inhabitants and in accordance with the principles of international law, constitute a permanent and inalienable objective of the Argentine people

[1656] In this regard, it should be emphasized that priority is given to seeking the resumption of negotiations on sovereignty, persisting before international and regional organizations and the international community in calling on the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to engage in dialogue in accordance with the resolutions and declarations of the United Nations (UN), the Organization of American States (OAS), and other international organizations

[1657] Following the Falklands War, bilateral relations with the United Kingdom were subsequently frozen, but were resumed following the Madrid Agreements of

[1658] At that time, a series of security and mutual trust measures were agreed upon, which over time led to the creation of a nascent process of bilateral cooperation and exchange

[1659] Despite this, Britain's failure to comply with the United Nations General Assembly Resolution 31/49 to ignored has persisted, manifesting itself in successive unilateral acts linked to the exploitation of natural resources such as fishing and oil

[1660] In recent years, Britain has been reluctant to meet in the South Atlantic Working Group—the body established by the Madrid Agreements to resolve all issues related to the agreed measures—thus closing off the possibility of discussing the sovereignty dispute

[1661] In this context, the bilateral defense cooperation agenda with the United Kingdom has been severely limited

[1662] Argentina believes that the situation described could become a risk to regional security, both due to the possibility of environmental catastrophes resulting from hydrocarbon exploration and exploitation activities—illegally and illegitimately initiated by companies under British licenses—and from the uncontrolled unilateral issuance of fishing permits

[1663] It also believes that the lack of mechanisms for monitoring and controlling weapons of mass destruction systems that could enter the South American peace zone could pose a risk

[1674] International Agreements and Mechanisms The transformation process is expressed in the institutional framework of the Ministry of Defense's international relations

[1675] In the past, international agreements between the Armed Forces predominated, establishing their specific guidelines and objectives, eventually receiving ministerial validation

[1676] This situation not only obscured a comprehensive defense policy framework, but also consolidated the operational design of the forces into silos

[1677] The new instruments are based on establishing clear objectives and guidelines that reflect the current principles of international defense policy within the framework of Argentine law, as well as identifying areas of common ground and mutual benefit

[1678] From an institutional perspective, the Ministry of Defense issues directives regarding international defense policy and conducts international relations throughout the jurisdiction

[1679] In this way, political leadership is located at the national strategic level, carrying out inter-ministerial relations and supervising the actions of the military strategic level and the operational strategic level under the responsibility of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, as well as those of the tactical-military level under the responsibility of the General Staffs of the Armed Forces

[1680] The framework thus ensures consistency between the general objectives established in international law and the specific actions contained in military understandings and specific projects

[1681] Regional Bilateral Agreements and Mechanisms Bilateral agreements with countries in the region establish permanent institutional mechanisms for cooperation and coordination, and may cover diverse topics, such as those related to academic, scientific, technological, industrial and commercial cooperation, institutional strengthening in matters of international defense and security, or the creation of binational peace forces or specialized combined companies

[1777] Disarmament, Non-Proliferation and Arms Control The Argentine Republic, in its objective of contributing to international peace and security, has adhered to the majority of agreements and conventions that limit or prohibit the use of conventional and mass destruction weapons

[1778] The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Trade, and Worship establishes disarmament and nonproliferation policy, and the Ministry of Defense intervenes within its jurisdiction in State actions aimed at fulfilling its international commitments regarding counterproliferation and transparency in the transfer of war and sensitive material

[1779] To this end, the national government created a General Directorate of Defense Material Control, whose primary responsibility is to "implement, disseminate, and oversee compliance by the Argentine Armed Forces with the Conventions, Treaties, and Agreements to which the Republic is a party regarding armament, disarmament, and related matters

[1780] This task is addressed in two areas

[1781] In the area of control of war and sensitive material, the application of treaties and conventions on weapons of mass destruction (nuclear, chemical, and biological) is monitored, and all aspects related to the control of the export of defense materials and technologies are addressed

[1782] The Directorate serves as Executive Secretary of the National Commission for the Control of Sensitive Exports and War Material. In another area, the Directorate monitors the implementation of treaties and conventions on conventional weapons (Ottawa Convention on Anti-Personnel Mines; Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons; and Registry of Conventional Arms and Small Arms and Light Weapons) in the area of national defense. It also coordinates the Working Group on Anti-Personnel Mines, through which international cooperation in this area is implemented within the framework of International Humanitarian Law

[1797] Part III Chapter XIV 239 Part III Chapter XV THE STRATEGIC PLANNING MODEL Global conflict is characterized by a multiplicity of variables and interests at stake, the complexity of the areas and actors involved, the difficulty in reaching comprehensive solutions and an uncertain evolution

[1798] This results in exceptional difficulty in addressing this problem according to traditional categories of analysis: conflict hypotheses

[1799] CAPABILITIES PLANNING Until the end of the Cold War, the certainty in identifying interests, actors and rules involved in international dynamics made it possible to foresee possible “threats” and the actions necessary to confront them, configuring future scenarios based on conflict hypotheses

[1800] This made it possible to reduce the number of scenarios to be analyzed, allowing for a relatively simple determination of the courses of action to follow and the means required in each case

[1801] As it has developed, international dynamics have evolved over the past two decades in a way that has rapidly condemned conventional analytical frameworks to absolute obsolescence

[1802] There is now a general consensus that future warfare will be based on a network-centric joint planning and decision-making system and effects-based military operations

[1803] Under this provision, the capacity planning methodology has been developed since the mid-1990s in the main countries of the world

[1804] Capability planning assumes an uncertain environment, so it only defines generic threats and prioritizes the development of flexible capabilities

[1805] In this way, it renounces identifying a priori adversaries or enemies of a state nature against which to reactively organize its military power

[1806] This approach allows us to avoid security dilemmas, thereby avoiding falling into self-generated arms races

[1807] Capability planning is also functional for thinking about and organizing a regional defense system, since it enables the determination of complementary contributions between different countries, obtaining synergies from the division of labor and collective effort

[1808] In 1998, the Law on the Restructuring of the Armed Forces already anticipated the probable development of a defense system within the framework of Mercosur, indicating that it should take note of its requirements.¹ With this rationale, in 2006, through the Directive on the Organization and Functioning of the Armed Forces, the strategic decision was made to adopt capability-based planning, with the Argentine Republic officially renouncing the methodology of planning based on conflict hypotheses

[1809] PEN Decree 1691/2006, of November 29, Directive on the Organization and Operation of the Armed Forces

[1818] PLANNING METHODOLOGY. CONFLICT HYPOTHESIS. Generic threat

[1819] Uncertain threat. Development of flexible capabilities. Versatile. Overcoming reactive logic. Trade-off between the level of internal capabilities and the level of external risk assumed. “Future warfare has three characteristics that are recognized worldwide: it is joint—the three armed forces work together, not separately as we did in the Malvinas; they normally work in a network, which makes them more agile; and operations are effects-based

[1820] This planning method we are now working with abandons planning based on conflict hypotheses, which was absolutely limiting and even irritating, because each hypothesis was normally associated with a neighbor

[1821] In today's world, aggression can arise at any time and we cannot even be sure that it comes from an aggressor in the traditional sense - it could be a pandemic, an earthquake, a tsunami, etc. " Vice Admiral Antonio Torres (Joint Staff of the Armed Forces) in the National Seminar on the 2010 White Paper on Defense "National Defense in Bicentennial Argentina", National University of Cuyo, Mendoza, August

[1822] DEFINITION OF CAPACITY In its generic meaning, a capacity is the ability to achieve an effect, which can be defined in terms of what, how, when, where and for how long

[1823] In an organization, capability consists of skills and resources that, when combined, enable a measurable result to be achieved by performing a task under certain conditions and with specific standards

[1824] It is generally recognized that in capability planning there is a permanent interaction between defect (vulnerability) and effect (capacity

[1825] The determination of capabilities (effects) should try to eliminate or at least minimize one's own vulnerabilities (defects

[1826] These capabilities, in turn, will lead to a military instrument design that meets them

[1827] In strategic planning, a capability results from a set of factors (material, infrastructure, human resources, information, logistics, training, doctrine and organization: MIRILADO) used based on doctrinal principles and procedures, and aimed at achieving a specific military effect

[1828] AREAS OF CAPACITY

[1829] Military strategic planning has identified six major areas of capability

[1830] The first four are systemic in nature and force multipliers that support the last two, which constitute the main mission and the subsidiary missions

[1831] The rationale is that each capability area can be disaggregated as necessary into contributing capabilities and military capability objectives

[1835] Through an orderly sequence of documents, it has established the institutional dynamics that articulate scenarios, capabilities, resources, risks, and force design

[1836] The Cycle begins with the approval by the National Executive Branch of a “National Defense Policy Directive” (DPDN

[1837] From that point on, and under the supervision of the Ministry of Defense, the Joint Chiefs of Staff proposes Military Strategic Planning, convening the planning bodies of the Armed Forces

[1840] Part III Chapter XV Capability Planning Capability planning has been making its way into the planning systems of the most important strategic actors, national or multinational

[1841] The traditional system of conflict-based planning was based on identified threats, allowing for reliable information about potential aggressors

[1842] This information, in turn, enabled the design of an optimal defensive strategy

[1843] Information such as human resources, weapons types, readiness levels, and the potential aggressor's operational doctrine (all available or accessible) formed the input for determining the necessary force structure

[1844] In traditional planning, potential aggressors were identified in advance and their methods of combat were known, so the objective of planning was reduced to compensating their forces (military balance

[1845] In capability planning, where there is no predetermined threat under uncertainty, planning focuses on scenario selection and defining a set of capabilities to address threats that may arise across a broader spectrum of possibilities

[1846] Capability planning evaluates programs and structures at different budget levels and different scenarios to adapt to the changing environment

[1847] Traditional force structure planning had the advantage of facilitating short-term planning of personnel, weapons systems, infrastructure, and deployment, but it presented the serious risk that if the strategic context changed radically, weapons systems and deployments could quickly become anachronistic

[1848] Capability planning prevents the means from determining the ends and the senseless perpetuation of weapons systems and organizations that might have made sense at some historical juncture

[1913] The objective of the transformation in this dimension was to articulate an integrated resource management system that would allow the translation of approved military capabilities into human, material, and infrastructure resources in an effective, efficient, and transparent manner

[1914] Achieving this objective required taking initiatives to overcome the fragmented and disjointed operating logic with which each force had traditionally planned and managed its self-sustainment

[1915] DIAGNOSIS OF THE LOGISTICS SITUATION OF DEFENSE In the twenty years following the restoration of democracy, there was a real reduction in budget allocations for the defense sector, which meant that resources decreased in relation to the values of the Gross Domestic Product, from 3.1% in 1983 to only 1.1% in 2003, and in relation to the expenditure budgets of the national public administration in the same annual period, going from 14% to 7.7%

[1916] This contraction of the defense budget, as explained in previous chapters, was not accompanied by political guidelines for resizing that would have made it possible to adjust the organization and operation of the military instrument to a new reality of resources

[1917] The absence of directives from the national strategic level that sought to provide rationality to the process of financial contraction was evidenced through a marginal participation of the Ministry of Defense and the Joint Chiefs of Staff in the consolidation of the budgets of the Armed Forces

[1918] Thus, while the Ministry of Economy was limited to automatically establishing annual budget limits and proposing a priori an inertial distribution among forces, the heads of these forces proceeded to distribute them in a compartmentalized manner and according to exclusive internal prioritization criteria

[1919] Consequently, and even more so due to the chronic restrictions on the quantitative magnitude of the budget, a qualitative transformation aimed at a more efficient application of the budget was imperative

[1920] More than two decades after the conflict in the South Atlantic, the Defense System had still not capitalized on the lessons learned regarding the organization and operation of logistical support in military operations

[1921] In fact, several of the core shortcomings identified in the so-called "Rattenbach Report" that had to do with logistics were still present, and without the beginning of a comprehensive and overcoming solution

[1922] Three logistics organizations continued to coexist, one for each armed force, which only provided endogenous support to their respective forces

[1923] Each of these companies plans and executes its supply, maintenance, transportation, and storage programs based exclusively on its specific needs, without seeking complementarities with the rest

[1924] In short, these were autonomous operating schemes, devoid of synergies, which not only affected the possibility of common use of inputs but also disregarded the benefits of their acquisition or production on a larger scale, as well as the comprehensive use of the resources and infrastructure available to the Defense System as a whole

[1925] Such disjointed atomization was evident in the persistence of distinct organizations, practices, and even standards for similar, if not identical, functions and activities

[1926] Consequently, fundamental decisions regarding general logistics, such as the enlistment or non-enlistment, incorporation or decommissioning of a weapons system, were left to the circumstantial consideration of changing leadership, with no structural orientation emerging beyond the criterion of replacing assets that were reaching the end of their useful life cycle

[1927] This resulted in an automatic reflex that failed to question the continued existence of the strategic reasons that had justified the incorporation of the original medium that was intended to be replaced

[1928] The diagnosis was similar for logistics associated with sustainment, revealing a chaotic multiplication of supply units, maintenance centers, warehouses, and general infrastructure to acquire and store identical supplies or maintain identical types and models of weapons

[2107] The Transformation of the Scientific Research and Technological Development System for Defense The process of transformation of the scientific research and technological development system included the redefinition of its organizational structure, functional relationships, procedures and sources of financing

[2108] Thus, since the middle of the first decade of this century, actions were implemented to progressively increase the levels of scientific and technological autonomy and to recover productive capacities for the provision of strategic inputs for national defense

[2109] The transformation was guided by the following guidelines: 1- The integration of the scientific and technological system into the strategic defense planning process

[2110] The establishment of a specialized political leadership body as the head of an integrated system of science and technology for defense

[2111] The internal coordination of all defense research and development components in pursuit of efficiency, synergy and unity of purpose

[2112] The external coordination of the Defense Scientific and Technological System with the National Scientific and Technological System and public and private entities through agreements, programs, and projects

[2113] Integration of Research and Development into Strategic Defense Planning Traditionally, due to the lack of an institutionalized cycle of strategic defense planning, there were no medium- and long-term equipment programs to guide the priority use of procurement channels, and in particular, research and development efforts

[2114] Thus, each armed force haphazardly drafted internal documents projecting processes for the incorporation and decommissioning of weapons systems, based on the subjective nature of its specific aspirations and on the objective foundation of the inexorable life cycles of its equipment

[2115] The R&D bodies of each force, therefore, had to program their efforts around changing operational requirements or focus exclusively on improving the performance of existing systems

[2116] The absence of an integrated model of a long-term military instrument prevented the conceptual detail of the weapons systems that would be required to be obtained over an extended period of time

[2117] With this tentative inventory, it would have been possible to determine which of them, for strategic reasons, would have been convenient to develop and produce in the country, which would have merited production in the country without their own development, that is, accepting the use of design licenses, and which could have simply been acquired on the international market without the need to consider technology transfer

[2118] The National Defense Strategic Planning Cycle includes, within its sequence, the development of the Long-Term Military Plan (PMLP), which includes the participation of the R&D system to meet certain military capabilities

[2119] These capabilities are proposed in the Military Capabilities Project (PROCAMIL) and approved in the Military Capabilities Plan (PLANCAMIL) once the adjustment to the medium- and long-term financial constraints provided has been made

[2120] For its part, the Ministry of Defense is developing a Resource Procurement Directive (DOM) that provides guidelines for prioritizing the various procurement channels

[2121] The synthesis of PLANCAMIL and the DOM gives rise to the Medium Development Plan, which allows for the establishment, over a long time horizon (thirty years), of the weapons systems that must be researched and developed at the prototype level, for subsequent local mass production

[2122] This is precisely the standard required by the defense science and technology system to organize itself, plan the training of its human capital well in advance, and invest in cutting-edge infrastructure and equipment

[2123] The strategic status of associated capabilities and technologies, access barriers, costs and development times, among others, constitute substantive elements of judgment when defining the variable degrees of control, logistical technological autonomy, and freedom of action appropriate for the Nation

[2124] Although the first Defense Planning Cycle will be fully completed in 2011, progress to date has allowed for the conceptual identification of seven Systemic Cross-Cutting Programs (vertical knowledge programs) to be prioritized by the defense R&D system. These programs are predominantly dual in nature and will contribute to increasing Argentina's national potential and strategic positioning on the regional and global stage

[2125] The seven Systemic Cross-Cutting Programs are: Cyberspace: technologies designed to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of essential information to maintain the operational continuity of cyberspace, which configures a new operational dimension—independent and omnipresent—in the terrestrial, maritime, and aerospace areas of jurisdiction and interest

[2126] Development of military devices, capabilities, organizations, and human resources that ensure the use and control of cyberspace specific to the components of the National Defense System, and those areas of associated strategic interest in the face of external attacks against national cyberspace (cyberwarfare

[2129] Development of specialized technologies that contribute to command and control, surveillance, exploration, and the acquisition and transmission of information in real time. Fourth generation conflicts: technologies to confront asymmetric aggression from external military state actors, in order to ensure: a. The integrity and control of information and communications networks by developing associated Information and Communications Technologies

[2130] b. The security and effectiveness – online and in real time – of the command, control, communications, computing, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance systems for the areas and fields of interest

[2132] d. Precision in one's own commitment and minimization of collateral damage in the face of the increasing urbanization of the conflict, particularly the development of unmanned vehicles, robotics, and non-lethal and intelligent weapons

[2133] against devices of mass destruction: technologies, systems and human resources to detect, monitor, verify, protect, disable and mitigate the effects caused by chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear weapons and/or devices, intended to ensure the survival of military elements as well as in civil protection operations

[2138] Creation of a Specialized Political Leadership Body Until the middle of the last decade, defense research and development activities lacked significant policies, plans, or budgetary resources

[2139] The activity was limited to isolated and unconnected undertakings within the armed forces

[2140] The lack of institutional coordination between the Ministry of Defense and the Joint Chiefs of Staff in the development of scientific and technological knowledge of interest prevented synergistic achievements and wasted the scarce scientific resources available

[2142] In this context, the introduction of a specialized political body emerged as a necessary condition to coordinate efforts related to common scientific knowledge and the development of technologies of joint interest

[2143] This led to the establishment of a framework for defining strategic criteria to guide the activities and resources of the research and development system cluster

[2144] With this rationale in mind, the Undersecretariat of Scientific Innovation and Technological Development was created in 2007. Since then, this body has served as the head of the Defense Research and Development System, determining—through the approval of plans, programs, and projects, and the evaluation and allocation of funding—the contribution of each R&D organization

[2145] Furthermore, it is responsible for coordinating and complementing these with the rest of the public and private sectors, in order to achieve the technological and material solutions required for national defense in general and for the operational needs of the military instrument in particular

[2146] Internal coordination of R&D organizations Given the original diagnosis of complete functional autonomy of the R&D organizations of each of the three Armed Forces, priority was given to the coordination and organic integration of all components under the jurisdiction of the Undersecretariat of Scientific Innovation and Technological Development

[2147] To this end, a series of structural reorganizations of the specialized agencies were first arranged

[2148] The National Meteorological Service (SMN), which until 2008 had been a military unit (strictly a simple General Directorate dependent on an Air Force command in the process of being transferred), was transferred to the Ministry of Defense

[2149] The limited meteorological needs of the force (basically for flight) had inhibited the SMN's foray into new fields of research such as climate change, among others

[2150] For this reason, it was decided to give the SMN a higher level of hierarchy by transforming it into a decentralized body and appointing its first civilian director in more than forty years. The Military Geographic Institute, once an exclusive body of the Army, had already been converted into a decentralized body and transferred to the Ministry of Defense in the 1990s, but it was improperly dependent on the Secretariat of Military Affairs and lacked guidelines

[2151] In this case, it was relocated to the Planning Secretariat, Undersecretariat of Scientific Innovation and Technological Development, and renamed the National Geographic Institute in line with an expansion of its scope

[2194] Since the end of the 2001 crisis, the State's industrial policy has focused much of its efforts on recovering and increasing the country's productive capacity

[2195] In the area of national defense, this entailed a revaluation of the sector's role in economic development through the reactivation of companies that were emblematic of the national industry and had been privatized or licensed in the 1990s

[2196] In addition to fulfilling its purpose of increasingly autonomously meeting the material requirements of the military instrument, the national defense industry must thus become an instrument for expanding the country's productive capacities, strengthening the virtuous interrelationship between the different areas of the State and between the State and the private sector

[2197] A political decision, within the framework of the national defense transformation process, has been to identify the State as the central actor in driving processes and in the creation and management of fundamental production entities

[2198] A constituent part of this definition is the requirement that said central actor must comply with precise and demanding organizational and efficiency guidelines, operate through highly professionalized organizations, with appropriate levels of technical and operational autonomy, and performance rules and objectives at the level of international best practices

[2199] Under this condition, and within the framework of the reconstruction of the sector's production capacities, the legal status of defense-related production establishments was not changed from limited companies

[2200] This decision is based on the fact that modern companies require agility in decision-making and subsequent implementation, flexibility in supplier and customer management, as well as high levels of technical autonomy in determining the policies to be followed in order to achieve the strategic objectives set by their main shareholder, the Argentine State in this case

[2201] The fact that the most significant productive experiences in the field of national defense are being led by government agencies in no way implies that current orientation and policy contemplate a defense production sector solely owned by the state

[2202] Private initiative must also play an important role in specific aspects, as it already does in some related activities

[2203] Since the beginning of the last decade, initially under the initiative and leadership of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces, and since 2008 directly under the leadership of the Ministry of Defense, the Symposium on Defense Research and Production (SINPRODE) has been held in the country

[2204] This biennial meeting is conceived as a forum for analysis, exchange, promotion, and formulation of proposals on the use of science, technology, and production as mechanisms for strengthening national defense and, simultaneously, promoting the country's technological and industrial development

[2205] With these premises, SINPRODE combines an exhibition of defense-related equipment and services with an academic section for theoretical debate, proposal development, and the study of experiences related to the topic

[2206] The largest defense technological and production complexes belong to the State and are represented by the companies that lead each of their specific productive branches—the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex (CINAR) and the Argentine Aircraft Factory (FAdeA)—or by projects that mark the direction of a particular area, bringing together and strengthening the interaction of actors with the capacity and resources to achieve common goals

[2207] These are projects developed and produced by the Armed Forces, such as the “Gaucho” light general-purpose airborne vehicle, or the secondary radars designed by INVAP, among others

[2377] Currently, AR-SAT provides telecommunications services to the Army and the Joint Chiefs of Staff through the Army's satellite teleport at Campo de Mayo, integrating the latter's territorial deployment with fixed and mobile stations

[2378] To illustrate the importance of the service provided by AR-SAT, it is worth noting that the Fortín Joint Task Force relies on this system to carry out air surveillance and control operations on the country's northern border

[2379] To support the joint and combined actions of the military in the context of land, sea, and aerospace, satellite communications play an important role in ensuring command and control

[2380] In this regard, the short-term requirements of the three Forces were consolidated, resulting in the need to integrate a satellite network that must include fixed, mobile, and onboard satellite stations, as well as global satellite communications systems to ensure the integration of land, sea, and air units

[2381] Construction of the SAC-D satellite in the company INVAP SE

[2382] Part III Thinking about the medium and long term, the need to operate in a network environment, where the speed of decision-making and the amount of information that must be exchanged will increase significantly, the military instrument clearly cannot remain alien to the possibilities offered by the domain of telecommunications to ensure the fulfillment of the primary mission and support to the community in disaster situations

[2383] The need for defense to have secure and efficient communications at all times and places requires sufficient material, financial, and human resources

[2384] In this regard, appropriate measures have been taken to train qualified technical personnel in the management and development of these technologies, and the joint telecommunications requirements of all secondary jurisdictions under the Ministry of Defense have begun to be consolidated

[2385] SPECIFIC PROJECTS GAUCHO PROJECT Regarding land resources, the development project for a Light Vehicle for General Air Transportable Use (VLEGA) continues, designed for exploration and transport tasks, with low cost, easy maintenance, high versatility and suitable for transport in a C-130 Hercules type cargo plane (six Gauchos can fit in its hold as they can be stacked

[2386] This project, an initiative of the Argentine Army and Ministry of Defense in cooperation with the Brazilian Army and Ministry of Defense, already has several prototypes manufactured and in operation

[2387] Currently, the project is in the final stages of testing, standardization, and certification, with the goal of beginning serial production of the vehicle in the near future

[2388] The Gaucho Light General Purpose Air Transportable Vehicle (VLEGA) is completing its approval process, after which serial production will begin to meet military demand and offer a commercial variant for potential civilian customers

[2389] PROJECT "HORNERO" The recovery of aeronautical capabilities is not solely focused on FAdeA. To carry out this modernization in the country, facilities at the 601st Aircraft Supply and Maintenance Battalion were built and adapted since

[2390] In addition, the necessary engineering and technology transfer was carried out, equipment and tools were added, along with a specific engine test bench, technical documentation was obtained, and the company's own personnel were trained

[2391] The conversion of the UH-1H helicopter fleet to the HUEY-II standard is carried out in strict accordance with the requirements and recommendations of the manufacturer of the spare parts and systems to be replaced

[2392] Some of the main benefits of converting to the HUEY-II standard are: - Increased maximum speed to 130 kts

[2393] Increased maximum takeoff weight to 9,500 lbs

[2394] Superior tail rotor control (approximately 50%

[2395] All Flight Safety Bulletins issued by the US Army are hereby released

[2396] Reduction of operating costs

[2397] Greater security for personnel and material

[2398] The manufacturer estimated the time for implementing the first kit was five to eight months, and the average work time for the company currently responsible for the conversion is four months

[2399] It took the Army three months and ten days to put the first Huey-II into flight, gaining the necessary experience to overcome any unforeseen events during the project's development

[2400] It should be noted that at this time there is no other workshop in the world, other than the manufacturer itself, authorized to perform the conversion of UH-1H to HUEY-II
